# Agent methods

Every method of the agent protocol (1409 methods), grouped by area, in the order the schema lists them. `agent.schema` returns the same table at runtime, and `regia mcp` exposes each method that has an MCP tool name as that tool. *Mutates* methods are rate-limited and need the permission shown in `.regia/agent.toml` (see [Safety](../agents/safety.md)). Parameters marked `*` are required. The *Guide* column links the agent-guide page that documents the method with examples.

Each area's second table is the method contract (ADR-1034): a typical call's params, the error codes the method can answer with besides the universal ones (`F0001`, `F0002`, `F0004`, `F0007`, `F0012`), the limits the dispatcher checks before the handler runs, and the cost. Array and string params without their own limit hold at most 65536 items or 1048576 bytes. *Heavy* calls also count against `heavy_rate_limit_per_second`. [Errors](../agents/protocol.md#errors) explains every code.

| `agent.job_status` | `job_status` | `read` | no | `job` (string), `id` (string), `since` (integer) | State, progress and streamed events of a long-running job by id (tests:<n> from agent.run_tests; render_out:<n> and dcc_bake:<id> forward to their own status methods). Poll with since = the last answer's next. Without job: every in-process job. | [jobs](../agents/jobs.md) |
| `agent.job_cancel` | `job_cancel` | `play` | yes | `job` (string), `id` (string) | Asks a running job to stop (a test run kills its cargo process; render_out:<n> forwards to render.out_cancel). Idempotent: a finished job answers its state. | [jobs](../agents/jobs.md) |
| `agent.run_tests` | `run_tests` | `build` | yes | `target` (string), `package` (string), `filter` (string), `exact` (boolean), `include_ignored` (boolean), `offline` (boolean), `dry_run` (boolean) | Runs one test target of the project (cargo test) off the protocol thread and answers a job id; agent.job_status streams each test's outcome and ends with the totals and failure output. Runs project code: needs the build permission. dry_run answers the command. | [jobs](../agents/jobs.md) |
| `agent.build_game` | `build_game` | `build` | yes | `profile` (string), `package` (string), `offline` (boolean), `dry_run` (boolean) | Builds the project (cargo build --message-format=json) off the protocol thread and answers a job id; agent.job_status streams each compiler diagnostic (file, line, column, message, code, suggestion) and ends with the totals, the artifacts and the command. Compiles project code: needs the build permission. dry_run answers the command. | [code](../agents/code.md) |
| `agent.hot_reload` | `hot_reload` | `build` | yes | `dry_run` (boolean) | Asks the running editor to rebuild the game crate and swap the new code in (its Compile action) and answers a job id; agent.job_status streams the progress and ends with the reload's structured outcome (accepted, phase, generation, detail, toast, elapsed_ms, types, instances, scripts_rebuilt, scripts_dropped). Rebuilds and runs project code: needs the build permission. editor_not_running outside the editor; hot_reload_busy while a reload runs. dry_run reports without building. | [code](../agents/code.md) |
| `agent.cook` | `cook` | `build` | yes | `platform` (string), `quality` (string), `clean` (boolean), `dry_run` (boolean) | Cooks the project's assets for a platform (regia cook --platform P --quality Q --json) off the protocol thread and answers a job id (cook:<n>); agent.job_status streams the cook's output lines as progress and ends with ok, exit_code, artifact (the pak directory), the CLI's JSON report, the output tail and the command. Desktop only (cook_desktop_only on Android). Runs project build scripts: needs the build permission. cook_bad_platform / cook_bad_quality name a bad value; cook_busy while a cook or package runs. dry_run answers the command. | [cook-package](../agents/cook-package.md) |
| `agent.package` | `package` | `build` | yes | `audit_dir` (string), `audit_artifact` (string), `platform` (string), `profile` (string), `container` (string), `confirm` (boolean), `dry_run` (boolean) | Packages the game for a platform (regia package --platform P --profile R --json) off the protocol thread and answers a job id (package:<n>); agent.job_status streams the build's output lines as progress and ends with ok, exit_code, artifact (the package path), the CLI's JSON report, the output tail and the command. Needs confirm: true (needs_confirmation otherwise) and the build permission. Desktop only (cook_desktop_only on Android); cook_bad_platform / package_bad_profile name a bad value; cook_busy while a cook or package runs. dry_run answers the command. audit_dir audits an existing project-relative package directory without building; the job report carries redacted hygiene findings, stable rule ids and hygiene.policy_digest. hygiene.complete, incomplete_reason, limits, peak_memory_bytes and work say whether every selected byte was checked and which memory, byte and work ceilings were in force. complete false is an incomplete audit; a policy failure has complete true and findings. allowance_obsolete marks a stale allowance (agents/package-hygiene.md). Shipping packages rewrite absolute build paths in text assets, drop internal notes, enforce stage_allow and refuse dev-feature markers or an accepted dev probe (build_path, internal_notes, stage_allow, dev_flag). audit_dir reports those rules and does not rewrite, delete or execute. audit_artifact audits a finished project-relative package file or directory in place (ZIP, APK, AAB, tar, tar.gz, nested .fpak) and the report's final_audit is its versioned receipt: artifact_hash, policy_digest, tool, coverage (containers, uninspected, complete) and hygiene. A shipping package writes that receipt beside its artifact and the job report's final_audit carries it with verified (agents/package-hygiene.md, ADR-8348). | [cook-package](../agents/cook-package.md) |
| `agent.open_in_editor` | `open_in_editor` | `play` | yes | `entity` (integer), `asset` (string), `file` (string), `line` (integer), `dry_run` (boolean) | Asks the running editor to show something to the humans watching: select an entity, open a prefab for editing, or open a project file at a line in the owner's code editor. The editor tries the preference code.editor_command first, then [editor] code_editor in .regia/agent.toml. open_in_editor_no_code_editor only when both are unset. Answers editor_not_running outside the editor. | [staged-review](../agents/staged-review.md) |
| `agent.golden_test` | `golden_test` | `build` | yes | `name`* (string), `dry_run` (boolean) | Runs a named golden image's test through the agent.run_tests machinery and answers a job id (golden:<n>). The finished job's result gives pass or fail, the paths of the expected, actual and diff PNGs, and the measured stats. It only ever compares: REGIA_BLESS never reaches the test, and no golden is written. Needs the read and build permissions (it runs project code). | [goldens](../agents/goldens.md) |
| `agent.bless_golden` | `bless_golden` | `assets` | yes | `name`* (string), `reason`* (string), `job`* (string), `dry_run` (boolean) | Proposes a finished agent.golden_test job's actual image as the new golden: stages before, after and diff in the review queue with the required reason. Writes nothing under any golden directory. No agent can accept the proposal, with any permission: only the owner does, at a terminal, with `regia golden accept <id>`. | [goldens](../agents/goldens.md) |

| `assets.font_subset` | `assets_font_subset` | `read` | no | `font` (string) | What the last cook did to the project's fonts (ADR-2697): per font, the mode (auto, off, locales), glyphs total and kept, bytes before and after, a warning code when it was kept whole (CFF, collection, color, no outlines, no localization, unreadable) and, per locale, the characters the locale's text uses that the font does not map. | `assets.texture_sets` | `assets_texture_sets` | `assets` | yes | `folder`* (string), `write` (boolean), `recursive` (boolean) | Detect PBR texture sets in a project folder and generate one .material.ron per set (spec 22 T2.14, ADR-3320): maps named <base>_<suffix>.<ext> (BaseColor/Normal/Roughness/Metallic/AO/ORM/ARM/RMA/MRA/Height/Emissive/Opacity, a shared table in regia_asset::texture_sets, extended by Regia.toml [import.texture_sets]) grouped per folder. Writes the members' .meta (cook usage, a DirectX normal's green flip, a packed map's channel order) and the materials with the textures' asset ids — but only with write: true, and never over an existing material (material_exists). Dry run by default. | [assets](../agents/assets.md) |

Read-only. | [voxel-far](../agents/voxel-far.md) |
| `assets.import_rules` | `assets_import_rules` | `read` | no | `path`* (string), `importer` (string) | The effective import settings of one source path, resolved from the project's config/import_rules.ron folder rules and the asset's own .meta (which wins field by field): the merged settings object and, per field, whether the .meta or which rule set it. Read-only; the same resolution the cook keys on, so a rule edit recooks exactly the sources it matches. missing rules file is not an error (no rules configured). | [import-rules](../agents/import-rules.md) |
| `assets.pak_diff` | `asset_pak_diff` | `tools` | no | `old`* (string), `new`* (string), `chunk_size` (integer) | What shipping the new build's paks over the old one's costs a player. Each side is a .fpak file or a packaged build directory (paks pair up by relative path). The summary reports per-asset changes by asset id (added, removed, changed by stored-bytes hash, moved: same bytes at a new offset, unchanged), the fixed-size chunk comparison (SteamPipe's public model: ~1 MiB chunks; default 1048576) and an estimated patch download in bytes — an estimate, not a measurement of a real Steam build, which also compresses and reuses depot chunks. Needs the tools permission (desktop tools class): the method reads arbitrary build paths. Codes: pak_diff_unreadable (a side does not open: missing, truncated), pak_diff_no_paks (a directory side has no .fpak files), pak_diff_invalid_chunk_size. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |

Default out: asset_ids.assetids.ron at the project root. dry_run: true lists the rows and writes nothing. Codes: asset_ids_bad_meta (a sidecar does not parse; an export never drops an id), asset_ids_write_failed, path_outside_project. | [asset-ids](../agents/asset-ids.md) |
| `assets.ids_import` | `assets_ids_import` | `assets` | yes | `file`* (string), `dry_run` (boolean) | Write the .meta sidecars an asset id manifest (.assetids.ron v1) records that are missing under assets/, with the recorded id and importer, so the next cook keeps the ids and a patch ships only what changed (regia cook --ids runs the same step). A source not on disk is skipped (missing_source); a sidecar with the recorded id is kept. A sidecar that names another id, or does not read, is never replaced, and two sources on disk never get one id: asset_id_conflict, nothing written, data.conflicts lists { path, recorded, existing, reason, shared_with }. Other codes: asset_ids_unreadable, asset_ids_invalid (bad text, newer version, unsafe or duplicate path, paths that differ only in letter case, nil id), asset_ids_write_failed, path_outside_project. | [asset-ids](../agents/asset-ids.md) |
| `assets.terrain_tiles` | `assets_terrain_tiles` | `read` | no | `asset`* (string) | Tile counts and the block encoding of a cooked terrain (ADR-5294). `asset` is the terrain layer path (assets/.../*.terrain.layers.ron) or the cooked index id. The heightfield, when present, reports its tile count; its samples stay R16, so its encoding is null. The encoding is the tile payload, not an index field. `source_grid` is the cooked count source's X/Z spacing and missing samples (index version 3, ADR-8871). Read-only. | [terrain-tiles](../agents/terrain-tiles.md) |
| `assets.texture_coverage` | `assets_texture_coverage` | `read` | no | `asset`* (string), `cutoff` (number), `channel` (string) | Per-mip alpha-test coverage of a cooked texture (ADR-3090): every level decoded with the runtime's CPU decoders (BCn, ASTC, ETC2 / EAC) and the fraction of texels at or above the cutoff (alpha, or red for a mask texture), with mip 0's coverage, the largest drop of any level of 64 texels or more, and preserved (drop within 2 %). The cutoff is the request's, else the source .meta's alpha_cutoff (a sidecar over 1 MiB counts as setting none; the read is capped), else 0.5. A far canopy that thins out shows as a falling coverage; set alpha_cutoff in the texture's .meta and recook. Read-only. | [texture-coverage](../agents/texture-coverage.md) |
| `assets.texpack_dry_run` | `assets_texpack_dry_run` | `read` | no | `path`* (string) | Checks a .texpack.ron channel-pack recipe without cooking it (ADR-3090, docs/formats/texpack-ron.md): the parse, each output channel (source.channel, 1 - source.channel or a constant), every source (image headers only, nested recipes followed, cycles found) and the output size under the size_mismatch policy, or ok: false with the recipe's texpack_* code and message. Read-only. | [texture-coverage](../agents/texture-coverage.md) |
| `assets.access_trace` | `asset_access_trace` | `read` | no | `limit` (number) | Recent environment-gated asset opens, pak reads and manifest lookups, plus trace sink health. | [asset-access-trace](../agents/asset-access-trace.md) |
| `assets.check_contract` | `check_contract` | `read` | no | `contract_ron`* (string), `observation`* (object) | Judge one asset observation against a .contract.ron (scale, axes, origin, LOD chain and budgets, joints, required nodes, sockets, clips, materials, textures, footprint and socket clearance). A wrong up axis or a missing socket is a finding, not a transport error. | [delivery-contract](../agents/delivery-contract.md) |
| `assets.diet_report` | `assets_diet_report` | `read` | no | `profile`* (string), `platform` (string) | What the cook diet did to a build profile's pak (ADR-8461, book/agents/cook-diet.md): the diet-report.json regia package --profile <name> writes beside the pak under [content.diet] and [profiles.<name>.diet]. textures: each texture a texture_caps glob (the first match wins) or default_max_edge caps, with the cap, the glob and the shipped size; lods: each mesh whose finest LODs the max_triangles ceiling dropped (largest first, never the last LOD); variants: each variant group with its pick (first or seeded), the members left out and those kept because a shipped asset depends on them; before and after: assets, cooked bytes and triangles; warnings with their codes. Read-only. | [cook-diet](../agents/cook-diet.md) |
| `assets.provenance_import` | `assets_provenance_import` | `assets` | yes | `records`* (array), `under` (string), `dry_run` (boolean) | Move pack provenance records (provenance/<pack>.toml: schema, pack_id, status, [[files]] rows with path, sha256, byte_len, origin, tool, generator, seed, created_utc, reviewer and two flags) into the provenance block of each source's .meta under assets/ (ADR-8834; .meta stays v2). Built-in fields map to the block; the hash, length, flags, tool label, pack id and status, a negative seed (seed_signed) and every unknown row field (voice rows: line_id, variant, text, voice, tts, take_approved_utc) are kept as extensions. A source not on disk (missing_source) or without a .meta (missing_meta) is skipped; rows naming one source twice are listed in duplicates. All or nothing: a hash or length mismatch, a .meta that does not read or already has another block, or differing duplicates answer provenance_import_conflict and nothing is written (data.conflicts, data.duplicates). A second run keeps every .meta (idempotent). Other codes: provenance_import_unreadable, provenance_import_invalid (bad TOML, schema above 3, unsafe path, a field that cannot be an extension key), provenance_import_write_failed, path_outside_project. | [provenance-import](../agents/provenance-import.md) |

## `registry.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `registry.query` | `registry_query` | `read` | no | `path` (string), `path_contains` (string), `type` (string), `tags` (array), `limit` (number), `refresh` (boolean) | Search the asset registry without loading any asset: every set condition must hold. `path` is a glob over registry paths (`*` inside a folder, `**` across folders), `path_contains` a substring in any case, `type` a cooked type path or its last segments, `tags` a list of "key" or "key=value" filters. Results are sorted by path; `total` counts every match before `limit`. The registry is the cook's asset_registry.bin (plus the registries next to mounted paks), re-read when it changes on disk or with `refresh`. | [asset-registry](../agents/asset-registry.md) |
| `registry.describe` | `registry_describe` | `read` | no | `asset`* (string), `refresh` (boolean) | One registry record by asset id or path: type, tags, cooked size, its direct dependencies (and the ids the registry has no record for) and the records that reference it. | [asset-registry](../agents/asset-registry.md) |
| `registry.dependencies` | `registry_dependencies` | `read` | no | `asset`* (string), `transitive` (boolean), `limit` (number), `refresh` (boolean) | What an asset depends on, from the cooked headers recorded at cook time: direct dependencies, or with `transitive` everything reachable (breadth-first, each record once, sorted by path per level). `missing` lists ids with no record. | [asset-registry](../agents/asset-registry.md) |
| `registry.referencers` | `registry_referencers` | `read` | no | `asset`* (string), `transitive` (boolean), `limit` (number), `refresh` (boolean) | What references an asset (the reverse of registry.dependencies): the records that name it, or with `transitive` every record that reaches it. | [asset-registry](../agents/asset-registry.md) |
| `registry.tags` | `registry_tags` | `read` | no | `key` (string), `refresh` (boolean) | Browse registry tags: every tag key with how many records carry it, or with `key` that tag's values and their counts. | [asset-registry](../agents/asset-registry.md) |

| Method | Example params | Error codes | Limits | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `registry.query` | `{"limit":20,"tags":["biome=forest"],"type":"CookedMesh"}` | `registry_bad_query`, `registry_bad_tag`, `registry_not_loaded`, `registry_unreadable` | `tags` at most 64 items; `limit` in 1..=5000; `path` at most 1024 bytes | light |
| `registry.describe` | `{"asset":"assets/props/tree.glb"}` | `registry_bad_query`, `registry_not_loaded`, `registry_unknown_asset`, `registry_unreadable` | — | light |
| `registry.dependencies` | `{"asset":"assets/props/tree.glb","transitive":true}` | `registry_bad_query`, `registry_not_loaded`, `registry_unknown_asset`, `registry_unreadable` | — | light |
| `registry.referencers` | `{"asset":"assets/textures/bark.png","transitive":true}` | `registry_bad_query`, `registry_not_loaded`, `registry_unknown_asset`, `registry_unreadable` | — | light |
| `registry.tags` | `{"key":"biome"}` | `registry_bad_query`, `registry_not_loaded`, `registry_unreadable` | — | light |

reachable is the union the cull used. debug_segments counts the overlay's lines. frame.sun_* is stage 3 (ADR-8414): sun_reached (cells the sun walk reaches through the portals), sun_walk_visits, sun_sealed_cells (covered by sun_cover and not sun-reached), sun_sealed_draws (draws inside a sealed cell's box, out of every sun cascade) and sun_dropped_draws (of those, shadow-only draws left out: no local light). sun_cover is the installed cover (cells, sun_direction) or null. frame.shadow_view_* is the shadow-view cull (ADR-8874): shadow_view_active (it ran: a shadowed sun, shadow_views on, no view seeing the outdoors unrestricted), shadow_view_tested (rigid sun casters of unreached cells), shadow_view_culled_draws (of those, whose swept shadow touches no reached cell's box and no outdoor frustum: out of every sun cascade) and shadow_view_dropped_draws (of those, shadow-only draws left out: no local light). shadow_views is the switch. terrain_sun_cover is the terrain's cover provider (grow_m, fills, cells_tested, cells_covered, last_grow_m) or null when off. | `render.set_viscells` | `render_set_viscells` | `edit_scene` | yes | `text` (string), `clear` (boolean), `cull` (boolean), `debug_draw` (boolean), `sun_cover` (array), `sun_direction` (array), `shadow_views` (boolean), `terrain_sun_cover` (boolean) | Installs or clears the indoor cells and portals and flips their switches. text is a viscells.ron document (version 1; validated first: a refused text changes nothing and returns its code, viscells_*); clear removes the cells (nothing is culled); cull false keeps the walk and its report but culls nothing; debug_draw shows the cells (green reached, red not, yellow the first view's cell) and portals (cyan) as gizmo lines (gizmo group viscells). sun_cover installs the cell ids whose boxes lie under cover that stays in the sun's cascades (with sun_direction, the sun's travel it was computed for; null or [] clears): a covered cell the sun walk does not reach is sun-sealed and its draws leave the sun's cascades (ADR-8414). shadow_views false turns off the shadow-view cull (ADR-8874: the draws of unreached cells whose sun shadow no view can see leave the sun's cascades; on by default). terrain_sun_cover true makes the terrain fill sun_cover itself from its min-max pyramid and holes for the frame's sun (a host sun_cover replaces it; false turns it off and clears the cover it filled). F0002 for a bad sun_cover, a missing or zero sun_direction, a wrong-typed switch, or sun_cover with terrain_sun_cover true. F0003 when debug_draw is passed without a renderer. Guide page: viscells. | [viscells](../agents/viscells.md) |
| `render.scene_hold` | `render_scene_hold` | `read` | no | — | The paused-scene hold (ADR-7890): whether it is on, and per window the newest frame's step (full, capture, held), its scene passes (0 while held), the held GPU time (composite plus UI; null until a timestamp sample resolved) and the running counts of held, captured and full frames. | [frame-pacing](../agents/frame-pacing.md) |
| `render.set_scene_hold` | `render_set_scene_hold` | `play` | yes | `on` (boolean), `refresh` (boolean), `follow_pause` (boolean) | Turns the paused-scene hold on or off (ADR-7890). On: the next frame renders the scene once and keeps it; later frames skip every scene pass and draw only the UI over the kept image. refresh: true renders one more scene frame and holds that one. Off: full frames from the next frame. Not persisted. | [frame-pacing](../agents/frame-pacing.md) |
| `render.dynres` | `render_dynres` | `read` | no | — | The app's dynamic-resolution governor (DynResGovernor): the permille it returns, whether it is held (it holds outside play, so menu and pause frames do not move the scale), the last frame's bound, the rolling median GPU time and its budget and range. present is false when the host installed none. | [frame-pacing](../agents/frame-pacing.md) |
| `render.load_budget` | `render_load_budget` | `read` | no | — | The runtime renderer's per-frame load budget and what it did on the last frame. budget: upload_bytes_per_frame and new_pipelines_per_frame (null: no cap), late (block: upload and build everything a frame draws now, the default; defer: work past a cap waits) and active (a cap under defer). last_frame: deferred_meshes and deferred_bytes (meshes left for a later frame), deferred_draws (draws skipped: mesh not resident or material-graph set still building), async_pipelines_pending (graph sets on their workers plus the engine's deferred variants, process-wide), admitted_meshes and admitted_bytes (uploaded under the cap), async_graph_sets (sets sent to the workers this frame) and bursts (runs of deferring frames since start). | [instant-load](../agents/instant-load.md) |
| `render.set_load_budget` | `render_set_load_budget` | `edit_scene` | yes | `upload_bytes_per_frame` (integer), `new_pipelines_per_frame` (integer), `late` (string), `recommended` (boolean), `reset` (boolean) | Sets the runtime renderer's per-frame load budget. With late defer, the meshes a frame references but has not uploaded are uploaded nearest first while the frame's mesh bytes are under upload_bytes_per_frame (the mesh that crosses it still lands), the rest on the next frames; a material graph whose pipelines would take the frame thread past new_pipelines_per_frame builds on worker threads. Their draws are skipped until ready (a late object appears a few frames later instead of a long frame). Absent fields keep their value, null clears a cap; recommended starts from 64 MiB, 8 pipelines, defer; reset from the default (block, no caps). Applies from the next frame; not persisted. | [instant-load](../agents/instant-load.md) |
| `render.draw_list` | `render_draw_list` | `read` | no | `limit` (integer) | The host's keyed draws: the regia_render DrawList resource, which extract_frame appends to the frame after the mesh entities, in key order, without one entity per draw. Returns the list's counts (items, hidden, skinned, chained: items with a LOD chain, local_casters, shadow_off, extracted: the meshes the last extraction appended, extractions), the last LOD selection of the chained items (lod: selected, color_lods and shadow_lods per LOD index, crossfading, selections; ADR-8457), items per render layer, and up to limit draws (default 64, at most 4096) in key order with key and object_key (16-digit hex strings: the object key is the renderer's per-object cache slot and temporal history), layer, visible, shadow (all, off or local), joints (skin palette length), lod_levels (chain length, 0 without one) and translation. present is false when the app has no DrawList. Draws from the list are not entities: render.visible_entities and scene.* do not list them. Guide page: draw-list. | [draw-list](../agents/draw-list.md) |
| `render.cluster_lod` | `render_cluster_lod` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entities`* (array), `target_triangles` (integer), `screen_size` (number), `dry_run` (boolean) | Build a vertex-cluster far LOD for a model split into pieces: the rigid meshes of every listed entity are clustered on one shared grid to about target_triangles in total, so every piece keeps its share and the seams between pieces stay closed, and the result is appended to each piece's mesh LOD chain as its coarsest level. max_error is the largest distance any vertex moved, which bounds how far the silhouette moved. dry_run reports without changing anything. | [cluster-lod](../agents/cluster-lod.md) |

## `play.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `play.pause` | `pause` | `play` | yes | — | Pause gameplay time (frames keep rendering). | [testing](../agents/testing.md) |
| `play.resume` | `resume` | `play` | yes | — | Resume gameplay time. | [testing](../agents/testing.md) |
| `play.step` | `step` | `play` | yes | `frames` (number), `timeout_ms` (number) | While paused, run exactly `frames` frames of game time, then answer. | [testing](../agents/testing.md) |
| `play.set_time_scale` | `set_time_scale` | `play` | yes | `scale`* (number) | Set the gameplay time scale (1 = real time, 0.5 = slow motion). | [testing](../agents/testing.md) |
| `play.inject_input` | `inject_input` | `play` | yes | `events` (array), `actions` (array) | Inject raw input events and/or action values (deterministic, replayable). | [testing](../agents/testing.md) |
| `play.wait_until` | `wait_until` | `read` | no | `condition`* (object), `timeout_ms` (number) | Block until a world condition holds (checked every frame) or it times out. | [testing](../agents/testing.md) |
| `play.expect` | `expect` | `read` | no | `assertions`* (array) | Evaluate assertions against the world now; returns a pass/fail report. | [testing](../agents/testing.md) |
| `play.get_diagnostics` | `get_diagnostics` | `read` | no | — | Frame rate, frame times, entity count and memory of the running app. | [testing](../agents/testing.md) |
| `play.hitch_report` | `hitch_report` | `read` | no | `seconds` (number), `warmup_s` (number), `drive` (string), `timeout_ms` (number) | Measure hitches over the next seconds (specs/27 § 2.4): frame-time percentiles vs p50, frames over 2 x p50, longest frame, CPU/GPU percentiles, frame-path device calls, pass/fail. | [hitches](../agents/hitches.md) |
| `play.frame` | `game_frame` | `read` | no | `max_width` (integer), `max_height` (integer) | The newest picture of the running game, scaled to fit max_width x max_height (aspect kept, never larger) and encoded as PNG, with the frame number it was taken on. From the renderer's next present, or from a FrameFeed in an app without a renderer. The editor's Game tabs stream it (ADR-7831). | [pie-net](../agents/pie-net.md) |
| `play.mute` | `mute_game` | `play` | yes | `muted`* (boolean) | Mute or unmute the running game's output (its root audio bus; the bus's own mute comes back on unmute). Without audio only the state is kept. | [pie-net](../agents/pie-net.md) |
| `play.freeze_state` | `play_freeze_state` | `read` | no | — | What the gameplay pause (Time::paused) holds right now (ADR-10105): the audio voices held on game buses and the exempt buses, the scene hold (on, follow_pause), a threaded sim host's hold, and how many video players hold their clock. Subsystems the app does not have are null. | [game-pause-freeze](../agents/game-pause-freeze.md) |

## `input.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input.rebind_state` | `input_rebind_state` | `read` | no | `context` (string) | The input rebinding state: the capture in progress (context, action, mode, device slot, step, prompt, inputs captured so far), the outcome of the last rebind (input and conflicting actions), why it was not saved, and every context's actions with their binding label, kind, whether the user overrode them, the capture modes they accept, the binding and axis tuning per device slot and the actions they conflict with now. | [input-rebind](../agents/input-rebind.md) |
| `input.rebind` | `input_rebind` | `play` | yes | `context`* (string), `action`* (string), `mode` (string), `slot` (string) | Starts a rebind capture: the next input rebinds the action (mode single: a key, mouse button, pad button, stick or axis; keys1d: two keys for a one-axis action; keys2d: four keys, up down left right, for a two-axis action; chord: a modifier then a key, for a button). Feed the inputs with play.inject_input. The new binding is merged into the live config and saved to user://input_overrides.ron. Errors carry data.code rebind_unknown_context, rebind_unknown_action, rebind_bad_mode, input_not_installed. | [input-rebind](../agents/input-rebind.md) |
| `input.rebind_axis` | `input_rebind_axis` | `play` | yes | `context`* (string), `action`* (string), `slot` (string), `dead_zone` (number), `invert_x` (boolean), `invert_y` (boolean) | Sets the dead zone and invert of an action's axis bindings (sticks, pad axes, key groups, mouse motion) on a device slot and saves them to user://input_overrides.ron. A field left out keeps its value. Only sticks and pad axes have a dead zone. Errors carry data.code rebind_unknown_context, rebind_unknown_action, rebind_bad_tuning, rebind_not_tunable, input_not_installed. | [input-rebind](../agents/input-rebind.md) |
| `input.rebind_save` | `input_rebind_save` | `play` | yes | `profile` (string) | Writes the live input overrides to a named profile (user://input_profiles/<name>.ron), or to the active file when profile is left out. Errors carry data.code rebind_bad_profile, rebind_save_failed, input_not_installed. | [input-rebind](../agents/input-rebind.md) |
| `input.rebind_load` | `input_rebind_load` | `play` | yes | `profile` (string) | Replaces the live input overrides with a named profile, which becomes the active one and survives a restart, or reloads the active file when profile is left out. A missing or corrupt file changes nothing. Errors carry data.code rebind_bad_profile, rebind_profile_missing, rebind_profile_corrupt, input_not_installed. | [input-rebind](../agents/input-rebind.md) |
| `input.rebind_profiles` | `input_rebind_profiles` | `read` | no | — | Lists the saved input profiles. Error data.code input_not_installed. | [input-rebind](../agents/input-rebind.md) |
| `input.rebind_cancel` | `input_rebind_cancel` | `play` | yes | — | Drops the pending rebind capture and any inputs it collected. Error rebind_not_pending when none is pending. | [input-rebind](../agents/input-rebind.md) |
| `input.rebind_reset` | `input_rebind_reset` | `play` | yes | `context` (string), `action` (string) | Resets one action to the project binding (with context and action), or every action when action is omitted, removes the overrides and saves. Errors carry data.code rebind_unknown_context, rebind_no_default, input_not_installed. | [input-rebind](../agents/input-rebind.md) |
| `input.spacemouse_status` | `spacemouse_status` | `read` | no | — | SpaceMouse devices (connected or unavailable with the reason), the last merged sample, the user config and the horizon-lock / dominant-axis toggles. | [spacemouse](../agents/spacemouse.md) |
| `input.spacemouse_inject` | `spacemouse_inject` | `play` | yes | `translation` (array), `rotation` (array), `buttons` (array), `frames` (integer) | Replace the SpaceMouse device state for some frames (normalised -1..1, before the dead zone); buttons fire their actions. | [spacemouse](../agents/spacemouse.md) |
| `input.spacemouse_nav_defaults` | `spacemouse_nav_defaults` | `read` | no | — | The fixed SpaceMouse navigation defaults every Regia Engine app shares (dead zone, curve, rates, pitch limit, button actions, override ranges). | [spacemouse](../agents/spacemouse.md) |
| `input.touch_controls` | `input_touch_controls` | `read` | no | — | Touch zones (button, floating stick) and gesture bindings that map touches to actions, which finger holds which zone, the actions held, and the fingers down. | [mobile-lifecycle](../agents/mobile-lifecycle.md) |
| `input.assists` | `input_assists` | `edit_scene` | yes | `set` (object), `clear` (boolean), `player` (number), `gamepad` (number) | The player's per-action input assists: hold (as authored) or toggle (one press latches the action on, the next turns it off), a minimum hold time (shorter presses never reach the action), auto-repeat while held (the action fires again after a delay, then at an interval) and a cool-down (evaluation steps that must pass after an accepted press). The default set applies to every player. player or gamepad (not both) reads and writes that overlay instead. With no parameters it only reports; set changes the named actions (null removes one), clear removes that set first. Persisted with GameSettings.accessibility like settings.set. Also lists the actions a toggle holds on for player 0. | [input-assists](../agents/input-assists.md) |
| `input.haptics` | `input_haptics` | `edit_scene` | yes | `rumble_scale` (number), `vibration_scale` (number) | The player's gamepad rumble intensity and phone vibration scale. Every rumble request (Gamepads::rumble or a RumbleRequest message) is scaled by rumble_scale. PhoneVibration::vibrate scales its amplitude by vibration_scale. 0 turns that channel off, 1 (the default) plays it as the game asks. Reduced motion does not change either scale. With no parameters it only reports. Persisted with GameSettings.accessibility like settings.set. | [input-assists](../agents/input-assists.md) |
| `input.glyph` | `input_glyph` | `read` | no | `action`* (string), `device` (string) | The button-prompt glyph a device family shows for an action (spec 11 section 7, ADR-7070): the project's InputGlyph table (assets/input/project.glyphs.ron) first, then the built-in families of the UI hint actions (activate, back, ...), then the action's first binding the device can press. source says which step answered. | [input](../agents/input.md) |
| `input.keyboard_layout` | `input_keyboard_layout` | `read` | no | `layout`* (string) | Read the physical-key preset for QWERTY, original Colemak or classic French AZERTY. Lists 30 letter-block labels and their physical codes, plus positional movement defaults. Does not change bindings or text input. | [keyboard-layout-presets](../agents/keyboard-layout-presets.md) |
| `input.pointer_claims` | `input_pointer_claims` | `edit_scene` | yes | `enabled` (boolean), `watch` (array), `expect_untriggered` (array) | The mouse buttons the runtime UI has claimed (ADR-7976): a press that starts over a hit-testable UI node belongs to the UI until that button's release, and action evaluation reads a claimed button as up, so a click on a widget never fires a gameplay action bound to it. On by default when UiPlugin is installed. watch arms a per-action counter of the frames gameplay saw each action; expect_untriggered then checks the watched actions stayed untriggered (check.passed). With no parameters it only reports. | [ui-input](../agents/ui-input.md) |

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `camera.get` | `camera_get` | `read` | no | `entity` (number) | The camera rig with the lowest entity id's mode, angles and target (or one by entity), the shared director's blend, and each local player's director shakes (players). | [framework](../agents/framework.md) |
| `camera.set_mode` | `camera_set_mode` | `play` | yes | `mode`* (string), `entity` (number), `follow` (string) | Switch a camera rig to a named mode (chase, overhead, first_person, free). | [framework](../agents/framework.md) |
| `camera.blend_to` | `camera_blend_to` | `play` | yes | `duration`* (number), `translation` (array), `rotation` (array), `target_entity` (number), `curve` (string), `player` (number) | Blend cameras to a pose or an entity over `duration` seconds along an easing `curve` (CameraDirector::blend_to): the shared director's rig cameras, or local player `player`'s PlayerCamera cameras. The pose is the target exactly at `duration`; a pose target holds until the next blend. camera.get reports the shared blend's progress as `blend`. | [camera-framework](../agents/camera-framework.md) |
| `camera.set_path` | `camera_set_path` | `edit_scene` | yes | `path`* (object), `shot` (string), `name` (string), `duration` (number), `fov` (array), `roll` (array), `rotation` (array), `dof` (any), `fade_in` (number), `fade_out` (number), `camera` (number), `play` (boolean), `preview` (number), `dry_run` (boolean) | Set a camera path: keyframed positions (linear, step or centripetal Catmull-Rom) and a look-at rule (heading, point or moving target). With `shot` it replaces that shot of the loaded sequence; without it, it creates a one-shot sequence and loads it. Optional fov/roll/dof tracks and fades; validates, previews sample points, supports dry_run. | [camera-paths](../agents/camera-paths.md) |
| `camera.raycast` | `camera_raycast` | `read` | no | `x` (number), `y` (number), `u` (number), `v` (number), `width` (number), `height` (number), `aspect` (number), `entity` (number), `ray_only` (boolean), `max_distance` (number), `layers` (array), `all_layers` (boolean), `cull` (string), `terrain` (boolean), `meshes` (boolean), `include_hidden` (boolean), `skip` (array) | What is under a point of the camera's image: turns a screen point into a world ray with the camera's pose and lens, then casts it over terrain and mesh layers like world.pick. CPU only; needs no window. | [camera-paths](../agents/camera-paths.md) |
| `camera.shock_shake` | `camera_shock_shake` | `read` | no | `distance_m` (number), `blast_frame` (integer), `energy` (number), `speed_m_s` (number), `reference_distance_m` (number), `max_amplitude` (number), `duration_s` (number), `yield_kt` (number), `shake_profile` (string), `mount_q` (number), `ceiling_deg` (number) | The shock-arrival shake schedule: fixed step, rate, shakes fired, shakes pending with their arrival frames. With distance_m it also reports what a blast that far away does: delay (distance / speed_m_s, default 343 m/s), arrival frame at the fixed rate, amplitude and the shake. | [fire-light-shock-shake](../agents/fire-light-shock-shake.md) |
| `camera.schedule_shock_shake` | `camera_schedule_shock_shake` | `edit_scene` | yes | `distance_m`* (number), `blast_frame` (integer), `energy` (number), `speed_m_s` (number), `reference_distance_m` (number), `max_amplitude` (number), `duration_s` (number), `yield_kt` (number), `shake_profile` (string), `mount_q` (number), `ceiling_deg` (number), `ground` (boolean) | Schedule the camera shake of a blast distance_m away: it fires into the camera director on the arrival frame (blast frame plus distance / speed_m_s, default 343 m/s, rounded up to a fixed step). scheduled is false when the shock is negligible at that distance. | [fire-light-shock-shake](../agents/fire-light-shock-shake.md) |
| `camera.shake` | `camera_shake` | `edit_scene` | yes | `preset` (string), `amplitude` (number), `frequency_hz` (number), `duration_s` (number), `falloff` (number), `origin` (array), `channels` (integer), `falloff_radius_m` (number), `travel_speed_m_s` (number), `yield_kt` (number), `player` (integer) | Send a camera shake to every camera whose shake sensor listens to its channels (read next frame). Noise presets bump, impact, rumble, explosion (overridable); blast (the shock law, arrival at 343 m/s) and ground (seismic wave and airblast). With origin the strength falls off over falloff_radius_m and arrives after distance / travel_speed_m_s, counted in fixed steps. Reports which cameras will feel what. With player, a noise shake goes to that local player's camera director only: just that player's cameras feel it (spec 14 B5). | [camera-shake](../agents/camera-shake.md) |
| `camera.shake_sensor` | `camera_shake_sensor` | `read` | no | `entity` (integer) | The cameras' shake sensors: each camera (rig, render camera, or any entity with a sensor) with the sensor it feels with (its own, the default of a rig or the shot camera, or none), and its pending and running shakes and the pose added this frame. Reports zone, blend, boom length and the round-trip state. With dt_s, steps that frame clock. With pivot and desired together, also returns the blend-shortened eye (no world sweep). Does not move a camera in the scene. | [interior-camera](../agents/interior-camera.md) |
| `camera.crane_state` | `camera_crane_state` | `read` | no | `entity` (integer) | What the Crane nodes of a camera driver's active rigs did last evaluation: base point, rail heading, the requested and the clamped axes (yaw, pitch in degrees, length in meters, mount yaw and pitch in degrees), which axes the limits moved, and the arm tip (the camera position). With entity, that driver only. | [camera-rail-crane](../agents/camera-rail-crane.md) |

## `level.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `level.open` | `level_open` | `edit_scene` | yes | `level`* (string), `mode` (string) | Opens a level at runtime through the world's LevelManager: "replace" (default) unloads the current level first, "additive" loads alongside it. Synchronous when the level's data is already in the LevelLibrary; otherwise the level is recorded Loading and completes when its data arrives (watch for LevelLoaded). | [runtime-gameplay](../agents/runtime-gameplay.md) |
| `level.unload` | `level_unload` | `edit_scene` | yes | `level`* (string) | Unloads an open level: fires LevelUnloading, then despawns its non-persistent entities. Unloading the current level promotes the remaining active level with the lowest id. A level that is not loaded answers { unloaded: false }. | [runtime-gameplay](../agents/runtime-gameplay.md) |
| `level.status` | `level_status` | `read` | no | `level` (string) | A level's load state and progress for a loading screen: progress is 1 once the level is active; while it loads, the resident fraction of its load set `level:<guid>` (0 without one, never 1 before it is active). Without `level`, every level the LevelManager tracks. `loading_screen` is the root entity of the project's loading-screen prefab while a Replace open waits (null otherwise). | [levels-layers-instances](../agents/levels-layers-instances.md) |
| `level.get_look` | `level_get_look` | `read` | no | — | The open level's look: exposure bias, EV clamp, meter and color grade. | [look](../agents/look.md) |
| `level.set_look` | `level_set_look` | `edit_scene` | yes | `look`* (object) | Deep-merge a partial LevelLook into the open level's look; the next frame uses it. | [look](../agents/look.md) |
| `level.get_baked_gi` | `level_get_baked_gi` | `read` | no | — | The open level's baked GI volume: the .fgiv it names (look.baked_gi), whether the framework installed it, who owns the volume in the renderer (level, host or none), the load error and its code (volume_not_found, volume_unreadable), and the renderer's baked-GI status. Since ADR-3006 also the split set (parts: how many are lit and each that did not load: the others stay lit; since ADR-3237 each lit part's bricks and how many are crops of a brick that crosses a cut), the layers that are the host's (host_layers), and the volumes' bytes against every memory tier (memory: what is over budget or past one binding, and what would fix it). | [baked-gi-maps](../agents/baked-gi-maps.md) |
| `level.get_baked_gi_stream` | `level_get_baked_gi_stream` | `read` | no | — | The baked GI volumes of streamed levels (loaded additively beside the open map): each one's level, path, fade weight (0-1), whether its level is still loaded, probes and load error with its code (volume_not_found, volume_unreadable); the stream settings; and the renderer's blend (its layers, volumes blended last frame, volumes dropped past the cap of 8 or the device's binding size). | [baked-gi-seams](../agents/baked-gi-seams.md) |
| `level.set_baked_gi_stream` | `level_set_baked_gi_stream` | `edit_scene` | yes | `fade_seconds` (number), `blend_distance` (number), `priority` (number) | Change how streamed levels' baked GI volumes join the blend: the fade time in and out, the blend distance (meters; 0 for tiles cut one probe column apart, the overlap for tiles baked with one) and the priority against the map's own volume (0). Unset fields keep their value. | [baked-gi-seams](../agents/baked-gi-seams.md) |
| `level.sample_baked_gi` | `level_sample_baked_gi` | `read` | no | `points`* (array), `normal` (array), `view` (array) | The blended baked GI light (irradiance / pi, per channel) and coverage at world points, as the renderer blends every installed volume, with the last frame's sun and fill; and the largest change between neighboring points. Sample a line across a seam between volumes to check it is continuous. | [baked-gi-seams](../agents/baked-gi-seams.md) |
| `level.export_bake` | `level_export_bake` | `assets` | yes | `path` (string) | Exports the open level's bake input: every GiMobility::Static entity with a MeshSource (mesh path + world transform; the one tagged terrain becomes the terrain mesh), the sun, sky and sky bodies of its atmosphere, and a probe layout, written as a .bake.ron v1 with a <name>.bake.stamp.json input-hash sidecar. Dynamic entities, static ones without a mesh and built-in meshes are skipped and counted. Errors carry data.reason: export_no_level, export_path_invalid, export_mesh_missing, export_terrain_ambiguous, export_no_input, export_read_failed, export_write_failed. | [baked-gi-export](../agents/baked-gi-export.md) |
| `level.storage` | `level_storage` | `read` | no | `level`* (string) | How a level is stored: the single file (.level.ron) or the directory form (.level.d/, one file per entity), its entity and file counts, and the editor's unsaved dirty set. | [levels-layers-instances](../agents/levels-layers-instances.md) |
| `level.convert` | `level_convert` | `edit_scene` | yes | `path`* (string), `to`* (string) | Convert a level between the single file and the directory form (lossless; the old form is removed). Refused while the editor has unsaved changes to the level. | [levels-layers-instances](../agents/levels-layers-instances.md) |
| `level.layers` | `level_layers` | `read` | no | `layer` (string) | The data layers of the open levels, ordered by name: kind, parent, requested and effective state (absent, parked, live), member count and peers; with how many members are despawned and parked now. | [levels-layers-instances](../agents/levels-layers-instances.md) |
| `level.set_layer_state` | `level_set_layer_state` | `play` | yes | `layer`* (string), `state`* (string), `recursive` (boolean), `side` (string) | Request a data layer state: absent (members not spawned), parked (spawned, hidden, not simulated) or live. A child layer is never more active than its parent. Applies at the next frame's layer switch. | [levels-layers-instances](../agents/levels-layers-instances.md) |
| `level.set_membership` | `level_set_membership` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity` (integer), `entities` (array), `add` (array), `remove` (array) | Add entities to or remove them from data layers (their LayerMembership component). | [levels-layers-instances](../agents/levels-layers-instances.md) |
| `level.placed` | `level_placed` | `read` | no | — | Every placed-level instance: the referenced level, inline or streamed, entities spawned, and the error that stopped it, if any. | [levels-layers-instances](../agents/levels-layers-instances.md) |
| `level.place_level` | `level_place_level` | `edit_scene` | yes | `level`* (string), `transform` (object), `mode` (string), `parent` (integer) | Place a loaded level inside the open level as one transformed object and fill it at once (inline: a child subtree with derived guids; streamed: an additive level parented under the instance). Cycles and nesting over 8 are refused. | [levels-layers-instances](../agents/levels-layers-instances.md) |
| `level.break_placed` | `level_break_placed` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity`* (integer) | Replace an inline placed-level instance with plain entities: derived guids become permanent, world transforms are kept, the source level is untouched. | [levels-layers-instances](../agents/levels-layers-instances.md) |
| `level.switch` | `level_switch` | `edit_scene` | yes | `path` (string), `cancel` (boolean) | Switch levels with cancel (ADR-8027): reads and parses a project level on a worker and opens it with Replace when it lands; the replaced level's parsed data leaves the level library and is freed on a worker, and the next read waits for that free, so one level is read or freed at a time. A switch while a read is in flight cancels that read. With cancel true it stops the read in flight and keeps the open level. Answers level.switch_status. | [level-switch](../agents/level-switch.md) |
| `level.switch_status` | `level_switch_status` | `read` | no | — | The level switch (ADR-8027): the source being read, the open level, how the last switch ended (opened, failed or cancelled), retire workers still freeing, and the counters (reads started, skipped before their turn, cancelled, landed, failed; retires; the longest wait for a free). | [level-switch](../agents/level-switch.md) |

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rules.get` | `rules_get` | `read` | no | — | The active GameRules: the concrete rules type's path, whether the match is over (its is_match_over), and the rules name the current level asked for (LevelSettings.game_rules, null with no level open), and match_session: true when MatchSessionPlugin steps the hosted match session from ECS. | [runtime-gameplay](../agents/runtime-gameplay.md) |
| `rules.match_get` | `match_rules_get` | `read` | no | — | The hosted match session (ADR-8102): the flow (paused, paused_by, paused_by_seat, between, seated, ready, observers, joins, starts_at, match_tick, step), the playlist, the objective board (mode, objectives, team_scores, match_over, end_reason, and locked: the locked objective ids, absent while none is locked), the current row, teams (defs, switch, rebalance_between_rounds, assist_window_ticks) and ledgers (rows, contributions), plus ready_counts, the board's mode id, and the phase, round, time_left_ticks and round_wins of the phase machine (ADR-8485). With co-op waves on, waves (settings, state with each started wave's planned, released and alive counts, lives_left and ended, plus alive, cleared and total); with a race course, race (settings, state with each racer's lap, checkpoint, remaining, lap_times, best_lap_ticks, place and dnf, plus standings in position order) (ADR-8695). GR-11.3/11.4: zone (null, or stage, phase, center, radius, target_center, target_radius, damage_per_tick and the schedule), placements ([{ team, place }], best first) and victory (conditions, surrender, alliances, last_standing, contenders, out, winners, decided, state). A client with no session answers from the replicated match views (source replicated). | [match-rules](../agents/match-rules.md) |
| `rules.match_setup` | `match_rules_setup` | `play` | yes | `settings` (object), `playlist` (array), `looping` (boolean), `order` (string\|object), `no_repeat_last` (integer), `playlist_id` (string), `phases` (object), `start` (boolean), `between` (boolean), `ruleset` (string), `options` (object) | Replace the match session with a new one (inserting the MatchRules resource when absent): settings, playlist rows and looping; start starts the first row at once, between opens the ready gate. | [match-rules](../agents/match-rules.md) |
| `rules.match_input` | `match_rules_input` | `play` | yes | `as` (object), `input` (object), `inputs` (array) | Apply flow inputs on the current lockstep step, in order: seat, ready, unready, observe, leave, approve_join (team, slot), pause (name), resume (name, host), host_pause (on), override_afk, open_between. as is the issuer seat; omitted, the caller is the host. | `rules.match_objective` | `match_rules_objective` | `play` | yes | `flag` (object), `hill` (object), `place_flags` (object), `zone` (object), `zone_rules` (object) | Place one objective on the board: a flag { team, position \| offset, id? }, the hill { min, max, id? }, place_flags { teams, offset, first_id? } (one flag per team at the symmetric bases), or a capture zone { min, max, id?, capture_ticks?, decay_ticks?, contest?, max_rate_units?, owner_scores_every?, owner_scores?, locked? } (ADR-8649); or set zone_rules { mode: domination \| hardpoint \| attack_defend, rotation?, rotate_ticks?, attackers?, defenders?, order?, score_limit? }. Ids default to free ids from 1000000. A zone shows kind zone and its zone { settings, owner, capturing_team, progress, locked, held_ticks, empty_ticks } on the board. | [match-rules](../agents/match-rules.md) |

| `rules.match_assign` | `match_rules_assign` | `play` | yes | `team` (integer), `slot` (integer), `unit` (integer), `from` (object), `group` (array), `counter` (object) | Seat a player or a party, or add a named counter on a seated row. {} seats one player on the smallest team. group is the party (first object is the request). counter is { team, slot, name, delta }. The three forms exclude each other. A refused team change answers match_team_switch_refused; a new counter past the cap answers match_stat_cap. | [match-rules](../agents/match-rules.md) |
| `rules.spawn_preview` | `match_rules_spawn_preview` | `read` | no | `player`* (integer) | Every PlayerStart for a player, in walk order (priority, then spawn order: PlayerStart arrival when the world tracks it, which PlayerPlugin installs, else position x, y, z; order says which, ADR-8704): its SpawnPoint side, tags, priority and enabled flag, whether it is eligible (refused: disabled, wrong_team, missing_tag or blocked) and its score terms (nearest_enemy_cm, enemies_in_sight, teammates_near, recent_uses, score), plus the start a pick would choose now (the session's spawn state does not move), the respawn settings and the running match's respawn book (ADR-8647). Set the policies with rules.match_setup settings.respawn { default, teams, spawn, seed }. Works without MatchRules (policy first). A missing entity answers spawn_player_missing. | [runtime-gameplay](../agents/runtime-gameplay.md) |
| `rules.match_report` | `match_rules_report` | `play` | yes | `tagged` (array), `holders` (array), `scores` (array), `defeat` (array) | The host's reports for the strategy victory conditions (GR-11.4): tagged unit counts per team (destroy_all_tagged), objective holders (hold_for), team scores (score_threshold) and teams the host puts out (defeat). The session evaluates them on its next played step. Every table is checked before any row lands; an empty or long tag answers match_victory_settings. Answers what rules.match_get answers. | [match-rules](../agents/match-rules.md) |
| `rules.end_stats` | `match_rules_end_stats` | `play` | yes | `as` (object), `note_kill` (object), `note_structure` (object), `players` (array) | The match-end ledger: start and over ticks, timeline lines and the length at the ledger tick rate. note_kill and note_structure are host-only. players adds team totals and the MVP (kills, then fewest deaths, then fewest ships lost, then lowest team, then name; an AI seat is skipped while a player exists). | [match-series](../agents/match-series.md) |
| `rules.series` | `match_rules_series` | `play` | yes | `as` (object), `length` (integer), `lives` (integer), `record` (object), `reset` (boolean), `rule` (string) | Read the best-of series and the win-rule lives. The host may set length (1, 3, 5, 7 or 9), reset, record a round { winner, carry? }, set lives (1..=10) and set rule (lives or structures). A guest who sends any of those is match_not_permitted and the series is unchanged. | [match-series](../agents/match-series.md) |
| `rules.vote_cast` | `match_rules_vote_cast` | `play` | yes | `as` (object), `now_tick` (integer), `option`* (integer), `voter`* (integer) | Cast or replace one ballot on the open end-of-match vote. A guest may cast only the voter id of their own seat (team<<8\|slot), and that check runs before the window. vote_closed when the window has passed. vote_bad_option when the option is not on the ballot. | [match-series](../agents/match-series.md) |
| `rules.vote_status` | `match_rules_vote_status` | `read` | no | `now_tick` (integer) | The open end-of-match vote: options, tally, winner and whether the window is still open at now_tick. A closed object when no vote is open. | [match-series](../agents/match-series.md) |
| `rules.ruleset_list` | `match_rules_ruleset_list` | `read` | no | — | Every loaded rule set in id order (the shipped tdm, ffa, ctf, koth and dom plus the project's assets/rules/*.rules.ron): id, name_key, the resolved skeleton, extends, builtin, the source path, the option keys and the content hash (16 hex digits) or the error that stops it resolving; errors lists the files that did not load (code, path, message). | [match-rules](../agents/match-rules.md) |
| `rules.ruleset_get` | `match_rules_ruleset_get` | `read` | no | `id`* (string), `options` (object) | One rule set as written and what it resolves to: the extends chain, the skeleton mode, the merged session settings, the zone rules, the win conditions, the option schema, the option values (the row's options over the defaults) and the content hash peers compare at the handshake. A bare skeleton id answers its Rust defaults with ruleset null. | [match-rules](../agents/match-rules.md) |
| `rules.ruleset_validate` | `match_rules_ruleset_validate` | `play` | yes | `text`* (string), `options` (object), `load` (boolean) | Parse and check a .rules.ron text (at most 256 KiB; the version is read first, unknown fields are refused) and resolve it against the loaded rule sets with options. load true also adds it to the app's registry. Errors carry data.path, the field the problem is in. | [match-rules](../agents/match-rules.md) |
| `rules.match_results` | `match_rules_results` | `read` | no | `since` (string), `limit` (integer) | Finished-match records under MatchResultsSettings.root, newest first: match_id, date, ruleset, map_id, end_reason, winner, draw, end { step, tick } and players per record, plus total, skipped and the writer's pending, written, failed and dropped counts. Only complete files are listed. | [match-results](../agents/match-results.md) |

| `sim.bridge_settings` | `sim_bridge_settings` | `read` | no | — | The sim bridge's presentation settings: handedness, teleport distance, presentation delay, each kind's blend policy (lerp \| snap \| hold) and the blend counters (ADR-8456). | [framework](../agents/framework.md) |
| `sim.host_restore` | `sim_host_restore` | `play` | yes | `bytes_hex` (string) | Debug builds only: restore a framed snapshot on the host thread and republish a still pair at its tick (ADR-8526). | [framework](../agents/framework.md) |

| `sim.set_bridge_settings` | `sim_set_bridge_settings` | `play` | yes | `handedness` (string), `teleport_distance` (number), `presentation_delay_ms` (number), `kind` (string), `blend` (string), `dry_run` (boolean) | Change the sim bridge's handedness, teleport distance, presentation delay or one kind's blend policy from the next frame; dry_run previews before and after. | [framework](../agents/framework.md) |
| `sim.det_debug_draw` | `sim_det_debug_draw` | `play` | yes | `what` (array) | Debug draw of the deterministic indexes: set what is drawn (grid, cell occupancy, candidate pairs, contacts, query shapes and hits, flow field arrows) and count the latest frame's primitives (ADR-8562, ADR-8839). | [det-ids-broadphase](../agents/det-ids-broadphase.md) |
| `sim.grid_flow` | `sim_grid_flow` | `read` | no | `goal`* (array), `profile` (integer), `window` (object), `max_cells` (integer) | A flow field on the host's deterministic grid (regia_nav::det::flow, published into DetFlowView): the direction byte and integer cost to the goal of every cell in a capped window, for a goal and a profile. A full field up to 1024 x 1024 cells, a clustered flow above; the last field is kept (ADR-8839). | [det-grid](../agents/det-grid.md) |
| `sim.state_hash` | `sim_state_hash` | `read` | no | `prefix` (string), `ignore` (array), `keys` (boolean) | Hash the world's simulation state: every reflected component of every entity as canonical text keyed <entity Name>/<Component> (map and set entries sorted, entity ids not included). Compare two runs of one seed and input at the same frame; keys: true adds a hash per key for sim.state_diff. nondeterministic lists what made this session not reproducible (an extension hot reload: nondeterministic_reload), empty when nothing did. | [determinism](../agents/determinism.md) |
| `sim.state_diff` | `sim_state_diff` | `read` | no | `against`* (object), `prefix` (string), `ignore` (array), `limit` (number) | Compare the world's state with the per-key hashes of an earlier sim.state_hash { keys: true } (from this run or another): the keys whose value changed, appeared or disappeared. | [determinism](../agents/determinism.md) |
| `sim.desync_rows` | `sim_desync_rows` | `read` | no | `to` (integer), `count` (integer), `against` (array), `split` (integer), `left` (string), `right` (string) | The per-system lockstep desync rows DesyncHashPlugin records after every step (one 64-bit word per named system: its serde components in entity-id order and its resources; the last 240 steps). With against (another run's or peer's rows, or lockstep systems row log lines) it names every system that split, the first step each did and the last step all agreed, plus the lockstep desync log lines. A diagnose ring (diagnose_raw) adds raw-bits words per row and names zero-sign or NaN-payload splits at their tick (report.float_bits); rows whose fold hit a failing Serialize are flagged partial (report.partial_from). report.unmatched lists rows the other side has no row for at that step (side left is this run, right the against rows). report.same is true only when report.verdict is same: some step was compared, no compared row was partial and neither the canonical nor the raw words split (verdict canonical, float_bits, partial or no_overlap otherwise; a partial step never counts toward last_agreed). Without an ECS desync hash the rows come from an external sim behind the threaded sim host (ThreadedSimHost::start_with_desync; source sim_host). Errors: no_desync_hash (F0003), bad_to, bad_count, bad_split, bad_label, bad_against, word_count. | [desync-hash-ecs](../agents/desync-hash-ecs.md) |
