| `anim.list` | `anim_list` | `read` | no | — | Every animated rig: state-machine state, parameters, root motion and ragdoll blend. | [animation](../agents/animation.md) |
| `anim.get_state` | `anim_get_state` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer) | One animator's runtime state: current state-machine state, the running transition (mode crossfade \| inertialize \| inertialize_spring, progress, inertial offset still decaying), parameter values and declarations, root motion, ragdoll blend, and what each StrideWarp / OrientationWarp graph node did on the latest frame (warps). | [animation](../agents/animation.md) |
| `anim.set_param` | `anim_set_param` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `name`* (string), `value` (any), `type` (string) | Set one anim-graph parameter (float, int, bool, vec2, vec3) or fire a trigger; the graph reads it next frame. | [animation](../agents/animation.md) |
| `anim.ragdoll_set` | `anim_ragdoll_set` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `mode` (string), `blend` (number), `blend_time` (number), `strength` (number), `tracking_time` (number), `recover_snap` (boolean) | Switch a ragdoll's mode (kinematic hit boxes, powered hit reactions, limp death) and tune it; a limp -> kinematic/powered switch is the get-up: bodies re-pin to the animation, the rig snaps to where the body lies and the fallen pose blends out. | [animation](../agents/animation.md) |
| `anim.ragdoll_hit` | `anim_ragdoll_hit` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `joint`* (string), `impulse`* (array), `reaction` (number), `recover` (number) | Hit a ragdoll: an impulse on the bone nearest a joint plus a decaying partial physics weight on that bone and its children (the hit reaction). | [animation](../agents/animation.md) |
| `anim.spring_list` | `anim_spring_list` | `read` | no | — | Every rig with spring bones (hair, tails, cloth strips): LOD state (frozen/reduced), binding problems, each chain's parameters and simulated joint positions in world space. | [spring-bones](../agents/spring-bones.md) |
| `anim.spring_set` | `anim_spring_set` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `chain` (string), `stiffness` (number), `damping` (number), `gravity_power` (number), `gravity_dir` (array), `hit_radius` (number), `enabled` (boolean) | Tune one spring chain (stiffness, damping, gravity, hit radius, enabled) without losing its simulation state, or switch a rig's spring bones on or off. | [spring-bones](../agents/spring-bones.md) |
| `anim.spring_reset` | `anim_spring_reset` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer) | Forget a rig's spring simulation; the chains re-seed from the animated pose next frame (after a teleport or a cut). | [spring-bones](../agents/spring-bones.md) |
| `anim.rig_attach` | `anim_rig_attach` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `ron`* (string), `morphs` (array), `dry_run` (boolean) | Compile a .drivers.ron (twist chains, helper joints, drivers, pose-space correctives) against a rig's skeleton and attach it; it runs after the animator, before the joints are written. dry_run only checks it. | [character-rig](../agents/character-rig.md) |
| `anim.rig_state` | `anim_rig_state` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer) | What the attached rig computed last frame: each driver's input and written value, twist rolls and helper angles (degrees), corrective kernel activations and material parameter outputs. | [character-rig](../agents/character-rig.md) |
| `anim.profile_check` | `anim_profile_check` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer), `profile` (string), `ron` (string) | Check a rig's skeleton against a skeleton profile (built-in generic-humanoid or vrm, or a .skelprofile.ron): missing and extra joints, hierarchy, humanoid roles, measured arm elevation against the rest-pose rule. | [character-rig](../agents/character-rig.md) |
| `anim.gait_validate` | `anim_gait_validate` | `read` | no | `path` (string), `text` (string) | Check a .gait.ron gait settings file (gap G7) the way the loader does: format_version first (newer is gait_version), the typed parse (gait_parse), the leg list (gait_legs) and the stepper's own validate (gait_settings, gait_pattern). A file that fails is ok false with its errors, not an RPC error. | [procedural-gait](../agents/procedural-gait.md) |
| `anim.morph_weights` | `morph_weights` | `read` | no | `entity` (integer) | Morph (blend shape) weights: one mesh entity's target names, weights, expression layers and packed GPU targets, or (no entity) every entity with morph weights, targets or layers plus the renderer's morph counters for its last frame. | [morph-weights](../agents/morph-weights.md) |
| `anim.set_morph_weights` | `set_morph_weights` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `weights` (any), `layer` (string), `mode` (string), `layer_weight` (number), `weight_param` (string), `remove_layer` (boolean), `clamp` (array), `normalized_sets` (array) | Set morph weights by target name or index. An entity whose weights are composed each frame (Animator or MorphLayers) takes them as an override layer ("agent" unless `layer` names one), so animation does not overwrite them; any other entity's MorphWeights are written directly. Layer edits (mode, weight, weight_param, removal), the clamp and normalized (viseme) sets go through MorphLayers. | [morph-weights](../agents/morph-weights.md) |
| `anim.gaze_get` | `anim_gaze_get` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer) | A rig's eye gaze: target, per-eye yaw/pitch against the limits, saturation, the eyelid-follow morph channels and the aim error. | [eyes-and-bind-poses](../agents/eyes-and-bind-poses.md) |
| `anim.gaze_set` | `anim_gaze_set` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `target` (any), `weight` (number), `convergence` (number), `saccade_speed` (number) | Point a rig's eyes at a world point or an entity (or null to rest); creates the gaze from the skeleton's eye joints when the rig has none. Also weight, convergence and saccade speed. | [eyes-and-bind-poses](../agents/eyes-and-bind-poses.md) |
| `anim.bind_pose_get` | `anim_bind_pose_get` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer) | Whether a rig has its own bind pose (per-instance proportions) and how its bone lengths differ from the shared skeleton. | [eyes-and-bind-poses](../agents/eyes-and-bind-poses.md) |
| `anim.bind_pose_set` | `anim_bind_pose_set` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `scale` (number), `bone_scales` (object), `clear` (boolean) | Give one rig its own proportions over the shared skeleton and clips: a uniform bone scale, per-joint bone scales, or clear to go back to the shared bind pose. | [eyes-and-bind-poses](../agents/eyes-and-bind-poses.md) |
| `anim.clip_report` | `anim_clip_report` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer), `clip` (string), `compression` (boolean), `position_tolerance` (number), `rotation_tolerance` (number), `scale_tolerance` (number), `propagated_tolerance` (number) | Health check of the clips a rig plays: key-data issues with stable codes (non_finite_key, unsorted_times, notify_outside_clip, ...), the root motion one loop adds, the loop seam (how far the last frame is from the first), the cooked foot-contact curves (contact.<foot>: keys, planted share, touchdowns), and the error the cook's compression leaves against the tolerances, measured on the rig's skeleton. | [animation-robustness](../agents/animation-robustness.md) |
| `anim.motion_match` | `anim_motion_match` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer), `speed` (number), `trajectory` (array), `candidates` (integer), `filter` (object) | One entity's motion matching: the feature database (clips, frames, feature groups and weights, k-d tree shape), the matcher settings (search interval, minimum time between jumps, transition cost, exclusion window, search method), what plays, the search and jump counts and the latest search (best candidate, continuation cost, jumped, held). With `speed` or `trajectory`, also a probe: the frame that path would pick from the playing frame, without changing the matcher. | [motion-matching](../agents/motion-matching.md) |
| `anim.motion_match_set` | `anim_motion_match_set` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `search_interval` (number), `min_jump_interval` (number), `transition_cost` (number), `exclude_window` (number), `stay_bias` (number), `loop_clip_bias` (number), `lockout_window` (number), `method` (string), `require` (array), `forbid` (array), `settings` (object), `trajectory` (array), `filter` (object), `weights` (object), `search` (string), `reset` (boolean), `scope` (object), `predict` (object) | Change one entity's motion-matching settings and tag filter: the search interval, minimum time between jumps, transition cost, exclusion window, stay and loop-clip biases, lock-out window, search method, and the `require` / `forbid` tag names a search must satisfy. Also the desired path, a `filter` object, newer settings (`settings` object), a runtime weight overlay, a search request and a reset; a montage-section `scope` filter and the trajectory predictor's inputs (`predict`, ADR-2858). Everything is validated before anything changes. Errors carry a bracketed code: motion_bad_number, motion_bad_method, motion_bad_tags, motion_tag_unknown, bad_setting, bad_weight, unknown_tag, bad_trajectory, bad_predict, no_predictor. | [motion-matching](../agents/motion-matching.md) |
| `anim.motion_match_database` | `anim_motion_match_database` | `read` | no | `entity` (integer), `database` (any) | Summarize a motion-matching database, by the entity that uses it or by asset path (a registered database, or a cooked .motiondb.ron the asset server loads): frames, dimensions (and padded to the eight-lane width), feature groups, clips, frames per tag, span counts, jump targets, normalization mode, hashes of the statistics and the content, k-d tree shape, median jump cost, build warnings, and which optional cooked arrays it carries (cooked_arrays: the per-frame clip speed and the clips with stored arc lengths; absent arrays are computed at runtime with the same result). Errors carry a bracketed code: unknown_database, corrupt_database, unsupported_version, missing_dependency, database_unreadable, bad_params. | [motion-matching](../agents/motion-matching.md) |
| `anim.mm_predict` | `anim_mm_predict` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer), `times` (array) | Read an entity's motion-matching trajectory predictor (ADR-2858): the desired velocity, the facing mode (velocity, or aim for strafing) and aim yaw, the critically damped spring state (position, velocity, yaw, yaw rate), the predicted path at the trajectory times in the character frame (what it writes into MotionMatching), and the recorded ground history, newest first. Errors: F0003 when the entity or its TrajectoryPredictor is missing; [bad_times] for bad times. | [motion-matching](../agents/motion-matching.md) |
| `anim.motion_match_databases` | `anim_motion_match_databases` | `read` | no | — | List the motion databases the app has registered, by asset path (cooked ones loaded through MotionDatabaseRef or anim.motion_match_database, and ones a host built in code), with their frames, clips, whether they can be played (skeleton and clips present), content hash and the entities whose MotionMatching uses them; plus the paths that failed to load with their reason codes. | [motion-matching](../agents/motion-matching.md) |
| `anim.montage_state` | `anim_montage_state` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer) | A rig's montage player: slots (group, joints), the montage library (sections and links, notifies, warp windows), playing instances (section, time, weight, phase), the queue, warp targets and the last 64 montage events. | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_play` | `anim_montage_play` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `montage` (string), `ron` (string), `rate` (number), `section` (string), `start_time` (number), `queue` (boolean), `reverse` (boolean), `duration` (number) | Play (or queue) a montage on a rig: a library montage by name or a whole .montage.ron document inline (added to the library). Adds a MontagePlayer when the rig has none. A playing montage in the same slot group is interrupted. | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_stop` | `anim_montage_stop` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `id` (integer), `blend` (number) | Stop one montage (by id) or all montages on a rig: they blend out, reported as interrupted; a full stop also drops the queue. | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_jump` | `anim_montage_jump` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `section`* (string), `id` (integer), `next` (string), `branch` (string) | Jump a playing montage to a section now; with `next` relink where that section goes at its end ("continue", "stop" or a section name; a section linking to itself loops); with `branch` arm the jump for that branching point. | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_set_warp_target` | `anim_montage_set_warp_target` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `name`* (string), `position`* (any), `facing_yaw` (number) | Set, move or clear a motion-warping target: while a montage's warp window for this name is active, its root motion is bent so the rig lands on the position (and turns to facing_yaw, or toward the position) at the window end. | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.sync_state` | `anim_sync_state` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer) | A rig's cross-node sync groups: the declared groups and sync markers (.sync.ron), and for each group that played last frame its leader clip, time, speed and looping. | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.warp_state` | `anim_warp_state` | `read` | no | `entity`* (integer) | A rig's motion-warp state: the warp targets of its montage player and of its scripted warps, each scripted warp (target, duration, elapsed, enabled, options) and its root-motion route. | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_describe` | `anim_montage_describe` | `read` | no | `asset`* (string), `slots` (string) | Read a .montage.ron (or a child montage, .montagevar.ron, resolved against its parent): tracks with each segment's clip range, rate, loops and timeline position (where the clip length is known), sections with links and follow links, notifies, warp windows, blends, the rate curve, slots used and issues (unknown slots against an optional slot table, clips of unknown length). | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_edit` | `anim_montage_edit` | `assets` | yes | `asset`* (string), `edit`* (object), `dry_run` (boolean) | Apply one edit to a .montage.ron file, atomically and validated (nothing changes on error), moving the notifies and sections linked to an edited segment (keep_time, shift_with_start, scale_with_length). edit.op: add_segment, move_segment (trim with start/end/to_clip_end, reorder with to, rate, loops), remove_segment, set_section, remove_section, link_sections, add_notify, remove_notify, set_follow, set_blend, add_warp, remove_warp, or undo (restores the text before the last edit; 16 steps per asset). A child montage (.montagevar.ron) takes set_override and remove_override only. | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_slots` | `anim_montage_slots` | `read` | no | `path`* (string), `montages` (array), `graphs` (array) | Read a skeleton's slot table (.slots.ron; a missing file is the engine default: one full-body slot `default`) and, per slot, the project's .montage.ron files and .animgraph.ron Slot nodes that play it. graph_issues lists Slot nodes naming a slot the table lacks (animgraph_unknown_slot). | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_slot_edit` | `anim_montage_slot_edit` | `assets` | yes | `path`* (string), `op`* (object), `force` (boolean), `montages` (array), `graphs` (array) | Edit a skeleton's slot table. op.op: add { name, group?, joints?, include_children? }, set { name, group?, joints?, full_body? }, rename { from, to } (rewrites every montage and graph Slot node that names the slot, all or none; refused when one is read-only), delete { name } (refused while montages or graph Slot nodes name it unless force). | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_control` | `anim_montage_control` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `id` (integer), `reverse` (boolean), `duration` (number) | Turn a playing montage around (reverse: true plays toward 0, false forward) and/or time-stretch the rest of it (duration: wall seconds from its current time to the end, rate curve included). | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.montage_commands` | `anim_montage_commands` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `record` (boolean) | The montage command hook (spec 34 § 9): read and turn on or off command recording on a rig's montage player. | `anim.scripted_warp` | `anim_scripted_warp` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `op`* (string), `id` (string), `target` (string), `duration` (number), `mode` (string), `translation` (boolean), `vertical` (boolean), `rotation` (boolean), `rotation_kind` (string), `rotation_fraction` (number), `offset` (array), `name` (string), `position` (array), `facing_yaw` (number) | Bend a rig's root motion toward a target for a while without a montage. op `add` starts a warp (an existing id restarts), `remove` deletes one, `pause_all` and `resume_all` hold and release every warp, `set_target` and `clear_target` manage the targets warps aim at. Adds a ScriptedWarps component when the rig has none. Finishing warps emit a ScriptedWarpEvent message. | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.root_motion_route` | `anim_root_motion_route` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `route` (string) | Read or set where a rig's extracted root motion goes: ignore (discarded), report (exposed through the animator but not applied), graph_and_montages (default) or only_montages (graph clips contribute none). | [montages](../agents/montages.md) |
| `anim.ragdoll_settings` | `anim_ragdoll_settings` | `play` | yes | `joint_limits` (boolean), `max_simulated` (integer) | Read, and with fields set, the ragdoll quality switch and budget: joint limits on or off (read when a ragdoll's bodies are built) and the most ragdolls simulated at once (settled ones beyond it freeze, oldest first). | `anim.crowd_status` | `anim_crowd_status` | `read` | no | `agent` (integer) | The crowd animation counters of the last fixed step (agents, archetypes with their gaits, step, poses evaluated, shared hits, agents updated and skipped, agents per LOD tier) and the output digest; with `agent`, that agent's tier, gait pair, blend weight, phase, playback rate, speed, yaw, position and hip ratio. | `anim.node_drivers` | `anim_node_drivers` | `read` | no | `entity` (integer) | Plain-node hinges, spins and slews: each drive's kind, axes, limits, input value and current angles. Omit entity to list every entity that has a NodeDriver. | [node-drivers](../agents/node-drivers.md) |

| `anim.gait_simulate` | `anim_gait_simulate` | `read` | no | `params` (object), `gait_asset` (string), `ground` (object), `inputs` (array), `body_path` (object), `steps` (integer), `dt` (number), `trace_every` (integer) | Run regia_animation's procedural gait stepper headless (stateless) over a seeded synthetic ground and answer quality metrics: max_foot_jump (largest move of any foot in one step) against swing_bound (the most a swing arc allows), max_planted_slip, min_planted, max_reach_ratio, refused, forced_steps, replants, settled, stability margins and a final pose hash; optional trace rows. inputs [forward, strafe, steer(, steps)] drive the integrating mode; body_path { points, speed } drives the driven mode. Errors: the stepper's gait_settings, gait_input, gait_state, gait_floor, gait_step_too_large, gait_pattern, plus simulate_too_long and bad_ground; with gait_asset also the loader's gait_parse, gait_version, gait_legs and gait_io. Guide page: locomotion-quality. | [locomotion-quality](../agents/locomotion-quality.md) |
| `anim.foot_plant_simulate` | `anim_foot_plant_simulate` | `read` | no | `settings` (object), `ground` (object), `speed_scale` (number), `yaw` (number), `steps` (integer), `dt` (number) | Run the foot planter (plant lock, tilt, smoothing) on the built-in demo humanoid's in-place walk while the rig moves speed_scale times the authored speed along -Z over a seeded synthetic ground (stateless), and answer max_slide (planted ankle over a stance), target_slide, max_penetration, max_float, max_tilt_deg, mean_tilt_deg, largest_step and pelvis_min. Errors simulate_too_long, bad_ground. Guide page: locomotion-quality. | [locomotion-quality](../agents/locomotion-quality.md) |
| `anim.ik_report` | `anim_ik_report` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `enable` (boolean) | Per IK graph node (TwoBoneIK, LookAt, ChainIK, BodyAim) of one rig, what its solve reached on the latest evaluation: residual (meters, or radians for look_at and body_aim), iterations, clamped, weight. Guide page: locomotion-quality. | [locomotion-quality](../agents/locomotion-quality.md) |

The first call attaches a read-only debugger to the entity; detach: true removes it. | [behavior-tree-editor](../agents/behavior-tree-editor.md) |
| `ai.statetree_validate` | `ai_statetree_validate` | `read` | no | `path` (string), `text` (string) | Lists every problem of a .statetree.ron (or of RON `text`) as { code, severity, path, state, message }: missing targets, duplicate names, unreachable states, unknown tasks (when tasks are registered), include cycles and the rest. Includes are read from the project. | [state-tree-editor](../agents/state-tree-editor.md) |
| `ai.statetree_edit` | `ai_statetree_edit` | `edit_scene` | yes | `path`* (string), `ops`* (array), `create` (boolean), `save` (boolean) | Applies structural edits to a .statetree.ron all or nothing, validates, and saves the canonical text atomically. Ops: add_state { name, parent?, index? }, remove_state { name, subtree? }, rename_state { name, to } (every transition target follows), reparent_state { name, parent, index? }, set_root { name }, set_state { name, selection?, enter?, weight?, utility?, clear_utility?, fallback? }, set_tasks { name, tasks }, set_ambient { tasks }, set_param { state, key, value? }, add_transition { state, trigger, condition?, target, priority?, hold?, index? }, remove_transition { state, index }, set_transition { state, index, trigger?, condition?, target?, priority?, hold? }, move_transition { state, from, to }, add_include { prefix, path, index? }, remove_include { prefix }, set_include { prefix, to_prefix?, path? }, set_tree { description?, seed?, state_key? }. A result with validation errors is refused (invalid_tree, data.issues) and the file is not written. | [state-tree-editor](../agents/state-tree-editor.md) |
| `ai.perception_hysteresis` | `ai_perception_hysteresis` | `play` | yes | `entity`* (integer), `sight_lose_radius` (number), `sight_lose_half_angle` (number) | Reads or sets one agent's sight lose cone (ADR-4586). Omit both lose fields to read. A present sight_lose_radius or sight_lose_half_angle is written only when the resulting pair is finite, at least 0, and no positive value is below the matching acquire range; otherwise the call answers perception_bad_hysteresis and both fields stay as they were. Zero means the acquire range. Guide page: perception-hysteresis. | [perception-hysteresis](../agents/perception-hysteresis.md) |
| `ai.team_knowledge` | `ai_team_knowledge` | `read` | no | `team`* (integer) | Facts one attitude-group team has shared: last known position and velocity, confidence, strength, sense and the agent that reported each one. A team with no facts is an empty list. | [ai-perception](../agents/ai-perception.md) |
| `ai.senses` | `ai_senses` | `read` | no | `name` (string) | The custom-sense registry: id, name, range, interval and confidence half-life. No name lists every registered sense. The built-in senses are not rows. | [ai-perception](../agents/ai-perception.md) |
| `ai.formation_get` | `ai_formation_get` | `read` | no | `squad`* (number) | One squad's formation: the built-in shape, the loaded asset path, the resolved slots and, when a crowd is installed, each follower's column state. | [ai-squads](../agents/ai-squads.md) |
| `ai.formation_set` | `ai_formation_set` | `edit_scene` | yes | `squad`* (number), `shape` (string), `asset` (string) | Sets a squad's formation to a built-in shape (ring, line, wedge) or a .formation.ron file. One of shape or asset. | [ai-squads](../agents/ai-squads.md) |
| `ai.debug_layers` | `ai_debug_layers` | `read` | no | — | The in-world AI debug layers, filter, radius, label cap, dropped-label count, watched blackboard keys and selected entity. Layers start off. The ai_debug gizmo group stays off until debug.set_gizmos enables it. | [ai](../agents/ai.md) |
| `ai.debug_layers_set` | `ai_debug_layers_set` | `play` | yes | `layers` (array), `filter` (string), `radius` (number), `label_cap` (integer), `selected` (integer), `watch_keys` (array) | Replaces the named AI debug settings. layers replaces the whole set (omitted names are off; an empty array turns every layer off). Unknown layer names answer unknown_layer and write nothing. filter is all, selected or radius; anything else is bad_filter and writes nothing. A present field of the wrong JSON type is F0002 and writes nothing. | [ai](../agents/ai.md) |

## `tilemap.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tilemap.list` | `tilemap_list` | `read` | no | — | Every tilemap entity: asset, size, tile size, tilesets, tile layers (tile counts) and object layers (objects with names, classes and positions). | [2d](../agents/2d.md) |
| `tilemap.get_tile` | `tilemap_get_tile` | `read` | no | `entity` (number), `x` (number), `y` (number), `world` (array), `layer` (string) | The tile at a cell (row 0 = top) or under a world point. A hit returns the GID, tileset, local id, flips, collision (empty/solid/one_way), class, properties, map rectangle, orientation and outline. An empty in-range cell (and an x/y past the map) returns cell and tile null. A world point outside the map returns tile null and reason. | [2d](../agents/2d.md) |
| `tilemap.set_tile` | `tilemap_set_tile` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity` (number), `layer`* (string), `x`* (number), `y`* (number), `gid`* (number), `flip` (object) | Writes one tile of a loaded map (a runtime edit; a hot reload of the source replaces it). `gid` 0 erases and ignores `flip` (the cell is stored as 0). Other gids take flips in `flip`. Errors: tile_bad_params, tile_bad_gid, tile_not_tile_layer, tile_outside_map. | [2d](../agents/2d.md) |
| `tilemap.autotile_register` | `tilemap_autotile_register` | `edit_scene` | yes | `name`* (string), `ron` (string), `path` (string) | Parses inline .autotile.ron text (docs/formats/autotile-ron.md), or loads the cooked .autotile.ron at `path` (from the pak), and registers it as an auto-tiling rule set under `name` (replacing one of the same name). Errors: tile_bad_params, tile_bad_rules. | [2d](../agents/2d.md) |
| `tilemap.autotile_list` | `tilemap_autotile_list` | `read` | no | — | Every registered auto-tiling rule set: its tileset, seed, border mode and terrains (layout, rule count, member tiles, variant entries). | [2d](../agents/2d.md) |
| `tilemap.paint` | `tilemap_paint` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity` (number), `layer`* (string), `rules`* (string), `terrain` (string), `erase` (boolean), `cells` (array), `rect` (array) | Paints a terrain of a rule set (or erases) over cells of a tile layer; the painted cells and their 8 neighbours re-resolve to the right edge/corner/inner tiles. Order independent and deterministic. Errors: tile_bad_params, tile_unknown_rules, tile_unknown_terrain, tile_bind_failed, tile_not_tile_layer, tile_outside_map, tile_too_many_cells. | [2d](../agents/2d.md) |
| `tilemap.autotile` | `tilemap_autotile` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity` (number), `layer`* (string), `rules`* (string) | Re-resolves every terrain cell of a tile layer through a rule set (after hand edits or an import). Errors: tile_bad_params, tile_unknown_rules, tile_bind_failed, tile_not_tile_layer. | [2d](../agents/2d.md) |
| `tilemap.stamp_copy` | `tilemap_stamp_copy` | `read` | no | `entity` (number), `layer`* (string), `rect`* (array) | Copies a rectangle of cells (inclusive corners, row 0 = top) of a tile layer as a stamp { width, height, cells } of raw gids with flip bits. Errors: tile_bad_params, tile_not_tile_layer, tile_outside_map, tile_bad_stamp. | [2d](../agents/2d.md) |
| `tilemap.stamp_paste` | `tilemap_stamp_paste` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity` (number), `layer`* (string), `x`* (number), `y`* (number), `stamp`* (object), `op` (string), `ops` (array), `skip_empty` (boolean) | Pastes a stamp with its top-left cell at x, y (signed; the part off the map is clipped), after the optional rotate/flip `op` or `ops` (the tiles' flip bits turn with it). Empty stamp cells leave the map alone unless skip_empty is false. Errors: tile_bad_params, tile_bad_stamp, tile_bad_gid, tile_not_tile_layer, tile_too_many_cells. | [2d](../agents/2d.md) |

## `replay.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `replay.load` | `replay_load` | `assets` | yes | `path`* (string) | Load a DO27 .do27replay (version 2, 3 or 4) into the world's ReplaySim (created when absent), rewind to tick 0 paused, and report the header, record counts, and the verification audit (state hashes are only checked when the player's codec can recompute them). | [replay](../agents/replay.md) |
| `replay.seek` | `replay_seek` | `play` | yes | `tick` (number), `seconds` (number) | Move the loaded replay to a tick (or second), clamped to the end, firing no events; returns the entity snapshot there. | [replay](../agents/replay.md) |
| `replay.step` | `replay_step` | `play` | yes | `ticks` (number), `presented` (boolean) | Advance the loaded replay by ticks (default 1, at most 36000, stopping at the end) and return the Moments, peer commands and abort crossed, each delivered once. The response lists at most 1000 events. | [replay](../agents/replay.md) |
| `replay.play` | `replay_play` | `play` | yes | `from_tick` (number), `speed` (number), `interpolate` (boolean), `max_gap_ticks` (number), `start` (string) | Play the loaded replay on the simulation clock from a tick at a speed, blending the presented entity poses between ticks for slow motion (seek and step snapshots stay exact). Under a render-out with a time_map the clock is the job's simulation clock, so speed composes with the map; start "render_out" waits at the tick and starts on the next render-out's frame 0, so every delivered frame is at from_tick + tick_rate * speed * sim_time. | [replay](../agents/replay.md) |
| `replay.pause` | `replay_pause` | `play` | yes | — | Stop frame-clock playback of the loaded replay where it is, and drop a replay.play start "render_out" arm. | [replay](../agents/replay.md) |

## `water.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `water.state` | `water_state` | `read` | no | — | Water bodies in the runtime frame: the plugin's switches, the tier in effect (low on Steam Deck, mobile and Desktop Low; high; ultra), the debug view, the deterministic water clock (fixed-step tick), what the last frame drew (bodies, triangles, obstacles evaluated, composited or blended) and every body (plane or ribbon, length, fall, width and speed range, obstacles, ice, look). | [water](../agents/water.md) |
| `water.probe` | `water_probe` | `read` | no | `at` (array) | What the water is at each point: the first body (entity order) holding it, the surface height, the surface flow (m/s) and speed, the lateral offset from a ribbon's centerline and its half width, the authored depth, the distance from the source, the Froude number and the wavelength of the waves that stand still against the flow. | [water](../agents/water.md) |
| `water.set` | `water_set` | `edit_scene` | yes | `enabled` (boolean), `tier` (string), `debug` (string), `running` (boolean), `tick` (number), `entity` (number), `look` (object), `ice` (any), `swell` (any), `terrain_planes` (boolean), `shore` (boolean), `ocean` (any), `ocean_draw` (boolean), `underwater` (boolean), `ring_culling` (boolean), `ring_snap` (boolean), `gpu_timing` (number), `sea` (any), `queries_follow_tier` (boolean) | Switch the water on or off, force a tier (auto \| low \| high \| ultra), pick a debug view (off \| transmitted \| reflected \| normal \| fresnel \| masks), hold or set the water clock, and edit one body's look (a field patch) or ice shelf (a field patch, or false to remove it). Everything is validated before anything changes. | [water](../agents/water.md) |
| `water.surface` | `water_surface` | `read` | no | `at` (array) | The visible water surface at points, at the water clock's tick: per point the highest wet surface over it among every body (level and swell planes, ribbons, terrain planes; ties go to the lower entity; spec 87), the height, the unit normal, the velocity of the surface water (swell orbital motion plus drift or flow), the crest foam (0..1, from the compression of the swell), the rest point on the still plane and the horizontal miss of the fixed-count inverse. A swell plane answers with every wave, whatever the tier draws; the drawn vertices near the camera lie on this surface within 1 mm. With a baked shore field (and shore on) the swell is shoaled and capped by the depth, dry land answers no body, and each answer carries depth_m, shore_m (distance to the shoreline), breaking and shore_foam (0..1); a ribbon reports its depth and bank distance. | [water](../agents/water.md) |
| `water.raycast` | `water_raycast` | `read` | no | `origin`* (array), `direction`* (array), `max_distance` (number) | The nearest crossing of a ray with any water body's surface at the water clock's tick: a march of 128 equal steps over the ray clipped to each body's box, then 24 bisections. Returns the distance, the point, the normal, whether the ray came from under the water, the march step (a crest thinner than it can be stepped over on a long grazing ray), the surface velocity and crest foam, and the depth, breaker and shore foam where a shore field knows them (no hit over dry land); hit false when there is none. | [water](../agents/water.md) |
| `water.floaters` | `water_floaters` | `read` | no | `entity` (integer) | Floating bodies (spec 87 § 5): each entity with a regia_terrain Floater, in entity order, with its sphere count and volume, fluid density and drag, and the last fixed step's buoyancy from regia_framework's BuoyancyPlugin: force and torque (world, about the center of mass), submerged volume and fraction, wet spheres and the water tick (state null before the first step or without the plugin). | [water](../agents/water.md) |
| `water.ocean` | `water_ocean` | `read` | no | `entity` (integer) | FFT oceans (ADR-1969): each plane body with a regia_terrain FftOcean, in entity order, with its authored fields, the sea state (significant height of this seed and of the spectrum, peak wavelength and period, the loop), each band's tile, wave-number range, mode count, variance and mean square slope on the query grid, and at the current tick the surface's reach, the share of folded texels and the map size the tier draws (0: the swell alone). | [water-ocean](../agents/water-ocean.md) |
| `water.ocean_check` | `water_ocean_check` | `read` | no | — | Compares the FFT ocean's compute pass with its CPU mirror (ADR-1969) on the GPU in use: reads the frame's maps back and returns the largest difference over every field of every band at the current tick. Blocks until the GPU is done. drawn false when no ocean is drawn (Low, ocean_draw off, no ocean body); F0003 without a water renderer. | [water-ocean](../agents/water-ocean.md) |
| `water.set_mode` | `water_set_mode` | `edit_scene` | yes | `mode`* (string), `entity` (integer), `grid` (integer), `ocean` (object) | Switches one plane body between its trochoidal swell and its FFT ocean (ADR-2126), keeping both setups: fft brings a parked ocean back, or the default one, with ocean (a field patch) and grid over it; swell parks the ocean, and queries and drawing go back to the swell, which a body without one gets from the ocean's stand-in. Validated before anything changes. Off by default: a body starts in swell mode. F0002 on a bad value or a ribbon; F0003 without WaterPlugin or without the body. | [water-ocean](../agents/water-ocean.md) |
| `water.ocean_cost` | `water_ocean_cost` | `read` | no | `grids` (array), `frames` (integer), `entity` (integer) | Times the FFT ocean's compute pass at each grid on the GPU in use (ADR-2126), on a simulation of its own, so the frame's maps are not disturbed: GPU time by timestamps where the device has them, wall time from submit to done, CPU time to set the grid up, modes and memory. The ocean is entity's, else the first body's, else the default. ran false when the device cannot run a grid, with refused naming the limit it exceeds (storage_binding, buffer_size, texture_dimension, workgroups; ADR-3251). Blocks until the GPU is done, for every frame; the times are measurements, not promises. F0002 on a bad value; F0003 without a water renderer, or when entity has no ocean. | [water-ocean](../agents/water-ocean.md) |
| `water.set_caustics` | `water_set_caustics` | `edit_scene` | yes | `enabled` (boolean), `strength` (number), `scale` (number), `speed` (number), `chromatic` (number), `shaft_steps` (integer), `tier_cost` (string), `shaft_accumulate` (boolean), `shafts_from_above` (boolean), `entity` (integer) | Edits one water body's caustics (ADR-2432) as a field patch: caustics on what lies below the surface (the sun's light focused by the ripples, from a 256 x 256 tile the GPU makes each frame) and sun shafts under it. Off by default, so default frames are unchanged; High and Ultra only (Low compiles the pass out, whatever is set). Validated before anything changes. F0002 on an unknown or bad field, a `low` tier_cost, or shaft_steps outside 0 and 8..=16; F0003 without WaterPlugin or without the body. | [terrain-water](../agents/terrain-water.md) |
| `water.caustics_stats` | `water_caustics_stats` | `read` | no | `depth` (number) | What the caustic passes did (ADR-2432): bodies with caustics on and active at the tier, the tile size, tile and shaft passes recorded, the shaft target; and, once a tile pass has run, the tile read back from the GPU and summarized at `depth` metres: the mean relative irradiance (near 1 by energy conservation) and the largest (the focusing). Blocks until the GPU is done when it reads the tile. F0002 on a bad depth; F0003 without a water renderer. | [terrain-water](../agents/terrain-water.md) |

## `tables.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |

| `tables.list` | `tables_list` | `read` | no | — | Every data table the game loaded (app.register_data_table): its asset path, row type, file form, row and column counts, generation (bumped by each reload and edit), reloads applied and refused, the error and warning counts of the last load, and the file it saves to. | [data-tables](../agents/data-tables.md) |

| `tables.get` | `tables_get` | `read` | no | `path`* (string), `key` (string), `keys` (array), `offset` (number), `limit` (number) | Rows of a data table as RON cell texts: one row by `key`, several by `keys`, or a page of rows in order (`offset`, `limit`, default 200). | [data-tables](../agents/data-tables.md) |
| `tables.set` | `tables_set` | `assets` | yes | `path`* (string), `key`* (string), `column` (string), `value` (string), `cells` (object), `remove` (boolean) | Edit a data table in the running game: set one cell (`column` + `value`), several cells at once (`cells`, all or nothing; a key that does not exist adds the row, fields left out take their defaults) or remove a row (`remove: true`). Values are RON literals (30, 0.5, true, Rifle, (x: 1)); a String column also takes plain text. The edit applies only when the row still parses and passes the game's row rules; it bumps the table's generation. tables.export with write saves it. | [data-tables](../agents/data-tables.md) |
| `tables.validate` | `tables_validate` | `read` | no | `path` (string) | Check data tables: duplicate and empty keys, the game's row rules, and the errors of a load or reload that failed (a refused reload keeps the old rows). Without `path`, every table. | [data-tables](../agents/data-tables.md) |
| `tables.export` | `tables_export` | `assets` | yes | `path`* (string), `format` (string), `write` (boolean) | A data table as `.table.ron` (v1) or RFC 4180 CSV text. With `write: true` the table is saved to its own file (atomic write; the live reload then sees the same rows), which needs a dev build with an asset server and the table's own form. | [data-tables](../agents/data-tables.md) |

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |

| `localization.status` | `localization_status` | `read` | no | — | The localization state: the selected locale, the source locale (the last fallback), the loaded locales, the selected locale's fallback chain (fr-CA, fr, en), the extra fallback edges from localization.ron, whether pseudo mode is on and the localization generation. Also how the start-up locale was chosen (the winning source of flag, environment, settings, steam, os or project, and its raw value), each locale's own name for language menus, and the font-fallback locale. | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |

A locale that is not loaded selects its nearest loaded parent (fr-CA selects fr when only fr is loaded). Texts re-resolve on the next frame and a LocaleChanged message goes out then. | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |
| `localization.resolve` | `localization_resolve` | `read` | no | `key`* (string), `args` (object), `locale` (string) | Resolves one message key the way the UI does: through the selected locale's fallback chain (or `locale`'s), with Fluent arguments (numbers select plural variants through Regia's CLDR table) and pseudo mode applied. Reports which locale provided the text, or missing. | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |
| `localization.set_pseudo` | `localization_set_pseudo` | `edit_scene` | yes | `on`* (boolean) | Turns pseudo-localization on or off: every resolved message gets accented letters, about 40 % padding and [ ] brackets, with placeables keeping their real values, so clipped or hard-coded text shows. Texts re-resolve next frame. | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |
| `localization.validate` | `localization_validate` | `read` | no | `strict` (boolean) | Runs the localization validator over the loaded locales: missing and untranslated keys along each fallback chain, extra keys, variable mismatches against the source locale, plural variants a locale lacks or never selects, duplicate keys. Content keys are not gathered here; run `regia loc validate` for the unused-key check. | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |
| `localization.plural` | `localization_plural` | `read` | no | `locale`* (string), `numbers`* (array) | The CLDR plural categories of a locale and the category of each number, from Regia's plural table (the same table the runtime selects with). Numbers may be strings to keep trailing zeros ("1.50"). | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |
| `localization.set_key_display` | `localization_set_key_display` | `play` | yes | `on`* (boolean) | Turns key display on or off (spec 36 § 5): every resolved text shows its key as ⟪key⟫ (⟪key name=value⟫ with arguments), so a tester sees which element uses which key. It wins over pseudo mode. Texts re-resolve next frame. | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |
| `localization.coverage` | `localization_coverage` | `read` | no | `locale` (string) | Translation coverage against the source locale, per loaded locale or for one: source messages, translated, untranslated, those with a gather placeholder, translations made against an older source text (stale) and the percent translated. | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |
| `localization.glyph_coverage` | `localization_glyph_coverage` | `read` | no | `locale` (string), `pseudo` (boolean), `charset` (boolean) | Which messages hold a character that no font of the running text system covers (the tofu-box check): per loaded locale or one, plus the pseudo-locale, each finding with the message id and line (code loc_glyph_missing); optionally each locale's character set for font subsetting. | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |
| `localization.set_audio_locale` | `localization_set_audio_locale` | `play` | yes | `locale` (string), `persist` (boolean) | Sets the spoken-audio locale (voice clips, localized sounds) apart from the text locale, or with locale absent clears it so audio follows the text again. The tag needs no text loaded. An AudioLocaleChanged message goes out next frame when the effective audio locale moved; persist stores it as the settings audio language. | [localization](../agents/localization.md) |

| `localization.resolve` | `{"args":{"count":3},"key":"menu-saves"}` | `bad_args`, `bad_key`, `loc_not_loaded`, `loc_unknown_locale` | `key` at most 256 bytes; `locale` at most 64 bytes | light |
| `localization.set_pseudo` | `{"on":true}` | `bad_flag`, `loc_not_loaded` | — | light |

## `net.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `net.status` | `net_status` | `read` | no | — | Every regia_net endpoint (server or client) the game publishes: role, state, addresses, tick and tick rate, peer count, conditioner settings and counters. bridge:false and no endpoints when the game has no NetAgentState. With the net runtime (NetPlugin) it also answers the process's mode, local peer, tick, connected peers and players (spec 70). A client that reconnects by itself after a timeout reports state "reconnecting" and reconnect { attempt, since_ms, next_in_ms, window_left_ms } (spec 120 § 10.3, ADR-8352). On a server, rejections counts what the runtime refused (server-only message types, malformed voice) and lists the newest 16 with the sender (spec 120 § 11.2). A server endpoint that did not resume a one-round-trip resume flight lists why in resume_refusals, a map from the lowercase refusal code (resume_epoch, resume_psk, resume_stale_flight, ...) to its count; totals carries resumed_one_rtt, resume_replays and resume_lapsed (wire 6, ADR-8902). | [net-trust](../agents/net-trust.md) |
| `net.resume` | `net_resume` | `read` | no | — | Replication-game resume on this server (spec 120 § 10.3): the dormant peers (timed out, PeerId and entities held for the grace window), and counters of resumes, takeovers, grace ends, on_grace_expired hook calls and verdicts, and held reliable messages kept or dropped. | [net-link](../agents/net-link.md) |

| `net.capture_save` | `net_capture_save` | `play` | yes | `path`* (string), `label` (string), `overwrite` (boolean), `stop` (boolean) | Writes the capture's whole sessions to a .netcapture (atomically: a temporary file, synced, then renamed). The capture keeps running unless stop is true. Replay it with NetLink::replay or the net soak's replay test. | [net-capture](../agents/net-capture.md) |

## `dcc_feed.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dcc_feed.status` | `dcc_feed_status` | `read` | no | — | The DCC scene feed: listeners, settings and every session (state, client, items, byte and frame counters, last error), replay and recording progress, warnings. Answers in every build. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |
| `dcc_feed.items` | `dcc_feed_items` | `read` | no | `session` (number), `kind` (string), `state` (string), `key_glob` (string), `limit` (number) | Items the DCC feed streams: key, stable guid, entity, kind, state, frame counters and size details (vertices, triangles, joints, channels). Filters combine. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |
| `dcc_feed.accept` | `dcc_feed_accept` | `edit_scene` | yes | `session`* (number), `remember` (boolean) | Accepts a pending DCC feed session: held declarations apply and the sender is asked to resync. `remember` allow-lists the client name in .regia/dcc_feed.toml. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |
| `dcc_feed.disconnect` | `dcc_feed_disconnect` | `edit_scene` | yes | `session`* (number), `despawn` (boolean) | Closes a DCC feed session. Its items stay as detached entities unless `despawn` is true. The kill switch of a runaway stream: always answers. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |
| `dcc_feed.record` | `dcc_feed_record` | `edit_scene` | yes | `action`* (string), `path` (string), `session` (number) | Starts or stops recording one DCC feed session to a .rfdrec file (relative to the project). A start asks the sender to resync, so the file stands on its own. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |
| `dcc_feed.replay` | `dcc_feed_replay` | `edit_scene` | yes | `path`* (string), `ticks_per_record` (number), `loop` (boolean), `as_client` (string) | Replays a .rfdrec as a new session on the fixed feed clock: the same file gives the same entity state at every tick. Progress is in dcc_feed.status `replay`. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |
| `dcc_feed.listen` | `dcc_feed_listen` | `edit_scene` | yes | `enabled`* (boolean) | Opens or closes the DCC feed listeners; closing cuts every connection. The editor panel's toggle. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |
| `dcc_feed.rotate_token` | `dcc_feed_rotate_token` | `edit_scene` | yes | — | Replaces the DCC feed token in .regia/dcc_feed/token. Open sessions keep running; new TCP senders need the new token. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |
| `dcc_feed.bake` | `dcc_feed_bake` | `assets` | yes | `items`* (any), `session` (number), `folder`* (string), `import` (object), `replace_live` (boolean), `dry_run` (boolean) | Bakes feed items into ordinary .glb assets through the normal importer. Answers a job id; dcc_feed.bake_status yields the report. `dry_run` answers the planned files and writes nothing. The editor provides it; every other build answers F0013. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |
| `dcc_feed.bake_status` | `dcc_feed_bake_status` | `read` | no | `job`* (number) | The state of a bake job from dcc_feed.bake. The editor frame applies a finished worker; this call only reports it. When the job is done, the reply is its report. The editor provides it; every other build answers F0013. | [dcc-feed](../agents/dcc-feed.md) |

## `procgen.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `procgen.list` | `procgen_list` | `read` | no | — | Every procedural generator: entity, guid, name, graph, mode, run state, run id, output counts (instances, entities, tables), whether it is stale, and its data layers and presence (its output is hidden while the presence is not live), and where a loaded bake came from. `bake_levels` names the levels whose bakes loaded (null: the opened level's directory; placed and additive levels by id) with counts from disk and from the pak, so a packaged game shows which levels' bakes its pak carries. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.get` | `procgen_get` | `read` | no | `entity`* (number) | One generator: its component fields, effective parameters with their source (generator, variant or default), effective seed, state, last error, and the bake its output loaded from (file, its directory, level, disk or pak, and kind: whole for a published output, cells for an anchored generator streaming its cells from the file, ADR-7287). | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.run` | `procgen_run` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity`* (number), `params` (object), `seed` (integer), `wait` (boolean), `keep_debug` (boolean), `threads` (integer), `timeout_ms` (integer) | Runs a generator. With wait:true it runs to completion in the call and answers the final state, output hash and counts; otherwise it queues the run (a run in flight is cancelled first). A scheduled generator (Anchored or Baked with tiles.runtime) is not queued: the call re-queues resident cells and returns the current run_id and state, with scheduled, requeued and run_requested. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.cancel` | `procgen_cancel` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity`* (number) | Cancels a generator's run in flight; the previous output stays. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.clear` | `procgen_clear` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity`* (number) | Removes a generator's output (spawned entities and instance sets), cancelling a run first. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.report` | `procgen_report` | `read` | no | `entity`* (number) | The last run's report: per node id, type, milliseconds, items, elements, cache hit, inactive, bypassed, warnings and counters, totals, and per road its length, junctions and flatten rect. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.inspect` | `procgen_inspect` | `read` | no | `entity`* (number), `node`* (integer), `pin` (integer), `item` (integer), `offset` (integer), `limit` (integer), `attributes` (array), `tier` (integer), `cell` (array) | A node's output items from the last run made with keep_debug:true: kind, tags, scope, length, columns and a window of rows. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.graph_get` | `procgen_graph_get` | `read` | no | `path`* (string) | A graph file (with unsaved edits): params, graph pins, nodes with settings, edges, flags, compile errors and the graph hash. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.graph_edit` | `procgen_graph_edit` | `assets` | yes | `path`* (string), `ops`* (array), `save` (boolean) | Edits a graph with ops applied in order (all or none; the result must compile): add_node, remove_node, set_setting, connect, disconnect, set_enabled, set_seed_salt, move, add_note, add_param, set_param_default, rename_param, remove_param, set_graph_pins, set_flags, set_description. Unsaved edits are kept as an overlay generators read; save:true writes the file. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.node_types` | `procgen_node_types` | `read` | no | `category` (string) | The node registry: type id, category, doc line, domains, pins with kinds, and settings with types, defaults, ranges and enum options. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.bake` | `procgen_bake` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity` (number), `cells` (array), `tier` (number) | Runs Baked generators (one, or all in the world) and writes their .pgout files to the bake directory; a tiled generator writes one section per cell, and `cells` re-bakes only those cells of `entity`, leaving the other cells' bytes unchanged. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.verify` | `procgen_verify` | `read` | no | `entity` (number) | Re-runs Baked generators without publishing and compares each output hash with its .pgout file (a placed member's in its source level's directory). Without entity, also names each entity that has a cell bake but lost its anchored generator (findings, anchored_generator_missing). | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.set_debug` | `procgen_set_debug` | `edit_scene` | yes | `tiles` (boolean), `regions` (boolean) | Toggles the runtime overlays: tiles draws each tier's cell grid colored by state, build and release circles around anchors, priorities on queued cells and cells with seam risk; regions draws generator bounds. Lines go to the gizmo group `procgen`. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.detach` | `procgen_detach` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity`* (number) | Editor only: turns a generator's output into ordinary level content (spawned entities lose Generated and are saved, instance sets become InstancedMeshSet entities, generated meshes become mesh entities, terrain edits stay applied) and clears the generator. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.tiles` | `procgen_tiles` | `read` | no | `entity`* (number), `tier` (number), `state` (string) | A tiled generator's cells: per cell its index, tier, state (queued, capturing, running, applying, resident, releasing, failed), instance count, run time and memory; the tiers, pool and resident memory. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.anchors` | `procgen_anchors` | `read` | no | — | The anchors anchored generation follows: the primary view and every ProcGenAnchor entity, with position, view direction and reach scale, plus any host-supplied extra anchors (ProcGenExtraAnchors, e.g. the editor's "generate around view" camera). | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.tiles_wait` | `procgen_tiles_wait` | `read` | no | `entity` (number), `anchor` (array), `tier` (number), `timeout_ms` (number) | Deferred: answers when every wanted cell around the anchor (or the current anchors) is resident, or fails with procgen_tiles_timeout. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.tiles_set` | `procgen_tiles_set` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity`* (number), `tier`* (number), `build_m` (number), `release_factor` (number), `view_bias` (number) | Live tuning of one tier's radii (not saved unless the editor saves the level). | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.tiles_rebuild` | `procgen_tiles_rebuild` | `edit_scene` | yes | `entity`* (number), `cells` (array), `tier` (number) | Re-runs the named cells (or every resident cell) of an anchored generator; a baked or on-load tiled generator runs again whole. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.plant_build` | `procgen_plant_build` | `assets` | yes | `graph`* (string), `out`* (string), `seed` (number), `variants` (integer), `params` (object) | Runs a Plant graph headless and writes its export jobs: one .glb per variant (LODs, wind attributes, impostor billboard, collision capsules) and a <name>.plants.ron index. Needs a host that links the asset pipeline (the editor). | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.plant_stats` | `procgen_plant_stats` | `read` | no | `graph`* (string), `seed` (number), `node` (number), `params` (object) | Runs a Plant graph in memory (nothing written) and answers per-plant statistics of a node's plant data: node count, max order, height, crown width, branches shed, triangles. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.wfc_solve` | `procgen_wfc_solve` | `read` | no | `size`* (array), `tiles` (array), `rules` (array), `sample` (object), `n` (integer), `symmetry` (string), `periodic_input` (boolean), `constraints` (array), `seed` (integer), `periodic` (boolean), `max_backtracks` (integer) | Runs Wave Function Collapse in memory (nothing read or written) on an inline tileset (tiles + rules) or sample grid (sample + n) and answers the solved grid: one tile or pattern id and one symbol per cell, x-fastest. At most 65536 cells. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.profile` | `procgen_profile` | `read` | no | `entity`* (number), `threads` (array) | Runs a generator's graph on its captured world once per thread count (0 = the serial schedule, n = a pool of n workers), each without the node cache and without publishing anything, and answers per-node wall times, the output hash of each run and whether all runs produced the same bytes (they must; spec 62 § 5.1). Timings are informational. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.load_report` | `procgen_load_report` | `read` | no | — | The level-load gate: whether a load is still generating (OnLoad generators' first runs, anchored generators with wait_on_load), what it waits for, and the last finished load's report (per generator: state, frames, ms, failure reason such as procgen_on_load_timeout). | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |
| `procgen.fingerprint` | `procgen_fingerprint` | `read` | no | `records` (array) | Digest of a procedural evaluation the caller already quantized, so two bakes compare without the world file. records is a list of { node, instance, position_mm: [x, y, z] millimeters, yaw_mdeg millidegrees }. Order does not matter. The answer digest is sixteen lowercase hex digits. An empty or omitted list has a fixed digest. More than 1048576 records answers procgen_fingerprint_overflow and does not mix. Nothing in the world is read or written. | [procgen](../agents/procgen.md) |

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |

| `stream.open` | `stream_open` | `play` | yes | `level`* (string), `mode` (string) | Opens a cooked streamed level from the mounted paks and the cooked cache: its always-loaded set spawns now, the cells stream around the sources. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |

| `stream.sources` | `stream_sources` | `read` | no | — | Every sampled streaming source and pin, with its world position. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.pin` | `stream_pin` | `play` | yes | `name` (string), `center`* (array), `radius_scale` (number), `priority` (integer), `ttl_steps` (integer), `wait` (object) | Adds a scripted streaming source at a world position. A wait counts in StreamStats.pending_waits until the region is ready. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.unpin` | `stream_unpin` | `play` | yes | `pin`* (integer) | Removes a pin. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.teleport` | `stream_teleport` | `play` | yes | `target`* (array), `move_source` (string), `wait` (string) | Pins a teleport target at the highest priority and waits for it. With move_source, that source's entity moves there once it is ready. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.ready` | `stream_ready` | `read` | no | `center`* (array), `radius_m`* (number), `readiness`* (string) | Whether every cell near a point reached a readiness level, and the cells it still waits on. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.budget_set` | `stream_budget_set` | `play` | yes | `budgets`* (object) | Changes any subset of the streaming budgets (development builds). | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.timing_set` | `stream_timing_set` | `play` | yes | `mode`* (string), `latency_steps` (integer) | Sets async or lockstep timing (development builds). Lockstep applies each load a fixed number of steps after issue, so a run repeats exactly. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.retry` | `stream_retry` | `play` | yes | `cell`* (string) | Lets a failed cell try again now, resetting its retry count. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.hlod` | `stream_hlod` | `read` | no | — | This frame's repaired HLOD cut and the holes in it; a proxy entry names the flat color it draws with. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.origin` | `stream_origin` | `read` | no | — | The floating origin: its cell, the rebase settings, the focus, what blocks a rebase and the last rebase. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.rebase` | `stream_rebase` | `play` | yes | `cell` (array) | Moves the floating origin on the next step (development builds); refused with stream_rebase_blocked while stream.origin names a blocker. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.trace` | `stream_trace` | `read` | no | `since_step` (integer), `limit` (integer) | The last streaming events, oldest first: queued, loading, applied, sim_ready, visible, unloading, unloaded, cancelled, failed, rebase. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |

| `stream.bounds_set` | `stream_bounds_set` | `play` | yes | `vram_bound` (boolean), `render_residency` (boolean) | Turns the VRAM planner bound (cells load only within vram_budget_bytes) and the render gate's residency wait (visible only once the renderer drew a cell) on or off. Both are off by default and also apply to levels opened later. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.collision_tiles` | `stream_collision_tiles` | `read` | no | — | Per-tile terrain collision counters: terrains built as tiles, tile colliders resident and pending, built and removed so far, cells held. | [streaming-runtime](../agents/streaming-runtime.md) |
| `stream.cell_relevance` | `stream_cell_relevance` | `read` | no | `peer`* (integer) | For one peer, the stream cells that peer has loaded, the one-cell margin, and how many replicated entities the stream_cells filter dropped on the last snapshot. An entity with no stream cell stays relevant. The filter only narrows. A dedicated server registers it when a streamed level is open; a client does not. Guide page: stream-cell-relevance. | [stream-cell-relevance](../agents/stream-cell-relevance.md) |

## `content.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `content.chunks` | `content_chunks` | `read` | no | — | Every content chunk of the build (content-manifest.ron): delivery, size, asset count, state on this device, requires and mount order; the sources in preference order. Empty with manifest false when the app has no content manifest. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.chunk` | `content_chunk` | `read` | no | `name`* (string) | One chunk: file, hash, delivery, state (with bytes while downloading), its first 100 asset paths and its size by asset type (from the chunk's registry when the chunk is on the device). | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.why` | `content_why` | `read` | no | `asset`* (string) | The chunk an asset (path or id) lives in and why: the cook's reason (rule, follows, shared, pinned, default), the rule selector that picked the direct asset, and the asset path chain back to it, from chunk-why.bin. Builds cooked without that file answer the chunk from chunk-map.bin with reason null. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.request` | `content_request` | `play` | yes | `chunks`* (array), `priority` (string), `allow_metered` (boolean), `mount_when_done` (boolean) | Request chunks (their requirements first, repeated names collapsed). Present chunks count as done; the rest are queued and transferred by the sources, a little every frame. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.progress` | `content_progress` | `read` | no | `request`* (integer) | Progress of a request: overall state and summed bytes, and each chunk's state and bytes. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.pause` | `content_pause` | `play` | yes | `request`* (integer) | Pause a request; transfers stop and keep their partial data. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.resume` | `content_resume` | `play` | yes | `request`* (integer) | Resume a paused request (request_not_paused otherwise). | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.cancel` | `content_cancel` | `play` | yes | `request`* (integer) | Cancel a request; partial data stays for a later request to resume from. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.approve_metered` | `content_approve_metered` | `play` | yes | `request`* (integer) | Let a request waiting for an unmetered network transfer now. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.mount` | `content_mount` | `play` | yes | `chunk`* (string) | Mount an installed chunk (and its installed requirements) at its manifest position; overridden live assets reload. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.unmount` | `content_unmount` | `play` | yes | `chunk`* (string), `force` (boolean) | Unmount a chunk; chunk_in_use while a load set pins its assets unless force, which removes those sets. Its loaded assets then read unavailable. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.release` | `content_release` | `play` | yes | `chunks`* (array), `keep` (array) | Delete fetched chunk files (and partial data) except keep; they become NotInstalled. Mounted, base and packaged chunks are chunk_in_use. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.set_source` | `content_set_source` | `play` | yes | `kind`* (string), `path` (string), `base_url` (string) | Choose where missing chunks come from: local (the content directory only), dir (a directory laid out like a static file host) or http (fetches <base_url>/<build_id>/<file>; https:// needs a build with the content-http feature, otherwise source_not_supported). | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.check_host` | `content_check_host` | `read` | no | `base_url`* (string) | Read what a chunk host offers (<base_url>/latest.ron, then that build's manifest) and compare it with the running manifest: chunks added, changed and removed. Changes nothing. It waits for the host, so use it from tools and deploy checks. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.inject` | `content_inject` | `play` | yes | `chunk`* (string), `fault`* (string), `after_bytes` (integer) | Debug builds: arm a deterministic fault for a chunk's next transfer: fail or stall after after_bytes, metered network, corrupt file, no space. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.network` | `content_network` | `read` | no | — | Whether the active network is metered: the platform's live answer (Android ConnectivityManager; null when it cannot tell, as on desktop, which transfers read as unmetered) and what the content manager uses (metered, whether its probe has answered, whether an injected metered fault holds it). Works without a content manifest. | [content-chunks](../agents/content-chunks.md) |
| `content.update` | `content_update` | `play` | yes | `base_url` (string) | Fetch the manifest a chunk host offers (<base_url>/latest.ron, then that build's manifest), check its detached signature (content-manifest.ron.sig) against the game's trusted keys before reading it, and adopt it: chunks whose hash changed read NeedsUpdate and the http source moves to the new build. On any error the running manifest is kept. Refused while a chunk is in flight or a mounted chunk would change. It waits for the host. | [content-trust](../agents/content-trust.md) |
| `content.check_placement` | `content_check_placement` | `read` | no | `objects` (array), `ground_y` (number), `half_extent` (number), `ground_tolerance_m` (number), `edge_tolerance_m` (number), `spawn_ring_m` (number), `spawn_rise_over_run` (number) | Check authored points against a flat height: on the heightfield, inside the map, unique ids, and a spawn ring under its rise limit. Empty params check nothing (ADR-8036). | [content-smalls](../agents/content-smalls.md) |
| `content.install_tier` | `content_install_tier` | `read` | no | `tier` (string) | The built-in install tier (minimal, low, high or ultra). Empty params return low. Residency caps, not a content list (ADR-8036). | [content-smalls](../agents/content-smalls.md) |

## `profiler.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `profiler.set_capture` | `profiler_set_capture` | `edit_scene` | yes | `flame` (boolean), `timeline` (boolean) | Turn flame (span call tree) capture and the per-thread timeline of the frame profiler on or off; at least one of flame and timeline is required. Both are off by default: each costs one record per span exit while on. profiler.frame, profiler.capture and profiler.timeline read the frames recorded while they were on. | [profiler](../agents/profiler.md) |
| `profiler.frame` | `profiler_frame` | `read` | no | `frames` (integer), `depth` (integer), `max_nodes` (integer), `since_frame` (integer), `entities` (integer) | The frame profiler over the newest frames: the CPU span call tree (per-frame mean inclusive and self ms, calls; most inclusive first), the ten costliest spans, and the main view's GPU pass times when timestamps are on. since_frame adds frame_times, every retained frame from that number on (a poller passes the last answer's newest_frame + 1 and sees every frame); entities adds the ECS counts with that many component types ranked by entity count. | [profiler](../agents/profiler.md) |
| `profiler.capture` | `profiler_capture` | `edit_scene` | yes | `path`* (string), `frames` (integer), `depth` (integer), `max_nodes` (integer), `timeline` (boolean) | Write a profile capture (.rprof.json, format profile-capture v2): the CPU call tree over the newest frames, the GPU passes and folded stacks, and the per-thread timeline of those frames when it was recorded, to a project-relative path. | [profiler](../agents/profiler.md) |
| `profiler.compare` | `profiler_compare` | `read` | no | `a`* (string), `b`* (string), `top` (integer) | Compare two profile captures (.rprof.json): per span (matched by its path from the root) the inclusive and self ms of a and b and b - a, largest change first; GPU passes likewise. Read-only and deterministic: the same files give the same answer. | [profiler](../agents/profiler.md) |
| `profiler.timeline` | `profiler_timeline` | `read` | no | `frame` (integer), `frames` (integer), `threads` (array), `max_spans` (integer) | The per-thread timeline of one frame the profiler retains (default the newest): per thread (by name) its spans with start and end in ns from the frame's start and the nesting depth. frames (1-8, default 1) lays that many consecutive frames, ending at frame, on one time axis: the spans keep their place on the axis and frames lists each frame with its start offset. Needs profiler.set_capture { timeline: true } first (timeline_off otherwise). Read-only. | [profiler](../agents/profiler.md) |

| `fluid.solids` | `fluid_solids` | `read` | no | `id`* (integer) | A fluid simulation's moving solids with the pressure impulse each got in the last step, and the coupled physics bodies (two-way coupling state). | [fluid](../agents/fluid.md) |

## `game.*`

| Method | MCP tool | Permission | Mutates | Parameters | Description | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `game.pause` | `game_pause` | `play` | yes | — | Pauses the game the way the player's pause key does (ADR-10104): gameplay time frozen (no fixed step, so physics, animation and AI stand still), gameplay input ignored, the cursor released and the game's pause screen shown. Refused with data.reason game_pause_off when the game did not turn the pause on ([game] pause = true), networked_session in a networked session (a peer cannot freeze the other players' worlds), game_pause_not_installed without GamePausePlugin; F0018 while a render-out runs. changed is false when already paused. play.pause is the raw time freeze for tests. Guide page: game-pause. | [game-pause](../agents/game-pause.md) |
| `game.resume` | `game_resume` | `play` | yes | — | Ends the game pause (ADR-10104): the screen goes, gameplay input and the cursor grab come back, and gameplay time runs again unless something else (play.pause, the focus-loss pause) froze it first. changed is false when the game was not paused. Errors game_pause_not_installed, F0018. Guide page: game-pause. | [game-pause](../agents/game-pause.md) |
| `game.pause_state` | `game_pause_state` | `read` | no | — | The game pause (ADR-10104): whether the game turned it on, whether it is paused (by input, screen, code or agent, since which frame), the TogglePause binding (key, gamepad, the label the screen shows), the screen setting and what shows, whether the session is networked, why a pause would be refused now, and counts. Read-only. Error game_pause_not_installed. Guide page: game-pause. | [game-pause](../agents/game-pause.md) |
